King Artaxerxes grants Ezra everything he requests.
Ezra is committed to studying, teaching, and observing the Law of the Lord.
Ezra is instructed to appoint judges and teach the people God's laws.

8.title: List of those returning with Ezra to Jerusalem.
Ezra proclaims a fast for safe travel and God's protection.
The group arrives safely in Jerusalem; temple offerings are made.

9.title: Leaders inform Ezra that the people, including priests, have intermarried with surrounding nations.
Ezra is deeply grieved; he prays and confesses Israel's sin.
Ezra recounts the sins of the people and seeks God's mercy.

10.title: The people gather and confess their sins; they commit to putting away foreign wives.
Ezra leads the people in an oath to separate from foreign marriages.
A committee is formed to investigate intermarriage cases.
Those guilty of intermarriage put away their foreign wives.

1.title: Nehemiah hears about the distress and broken walls of Jerusalem.
He mourns, fasts, and prays, confessing Israel's sins and seeking God's favor.
Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer, prays for success before the king.

2.title: King Artaxerxes notices Nehemiah's sadness; Nehemiah requests permission to rebuild Jerusalem.
The king grants permission and provides letters for safe passage and materials.
Nehemiah inspects the walls secretly at night.
He calls the people to rebuild the walls; they agree to start the work.

3.title: Detailed account of the families and groups repairing different sections of Jerusalem's wall.
Some nobles refuse to help, but many others work diligently.

4.title: Sanballat and Tobiah mock and oppose the rebuilding efforts.
The people continue building with all their heart; the wall reaches half its height.
Nehemiah sets a guard day and night against the threats.
Half of the men work while the other half guard; builders work with weapons in hand.

5.title: Nehemiah confronts the wealthy Jews exploiting their poorer brothers through loans and mortgages.
He rebukes the nobles and officials, calling for the return of fields, vineyards, and money.
Nehemiah sets an example by refusing the governor's allowance and not burdening the people.

6.title: Sanballat and Tobiah plot to harm Nehemiah by inviting him to meet.
Nehemiah prays for strength and continues the work.
The wall is completed in fifty-two days, despite opposition.
Enemies are disheartened, realizing the work was done with God's help.

7.title: Nehemiah appoints gatekeepers, singers, and Levites.
Genealogy of those who returned from exile is recorded to repopulate Jerusalem.

8.title: The people gather; Ezra reads the Book of the Law aloud to the assembly.
Levites help explain the Law; the people weep upon hearing it.
Nehemiah encourages joy; the people celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

9.title: The Israelites fast, confess their sins, and worship God.
Levites lead a prayer recounting Israel's history and God's faithfulness.
The people make a binding agreement to follow God's Law.

10.title: Leaders, Levites, and priests sign the covenant to obey God's commands.
People pledge to avoid intermarriage, observe the Sabbath, and support the temple.

11.title: Lots are cast to determine who will live in Jerusalem.
Lists of leaders, priests, Levites, and gatekeepers residing in Jerusalem.

12.title: The wall is dedicated with songs of thanksgiving and joyful celebrations.
Two choirs give thanks while marching on top of the wall.
Nehemiah appoints men to manage offerings, firstfruits, and tithes for temple workers.

13.title: Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem and finds Tobiah occupying a temple room; he removes him.
He confronts neglect of the Levites and restores tithes and support for them.
Nehemiah rebukes those violating the Sabbath by working and trading.
Nehemiah deals with intermarriage and purifies the people, restoring their commitment to God.

1.title: King Xerxes of Persia holds a great banquet in Susa.
Queen Vashti refuses to appear before the king; Xerxes is furious.
Vashti is deposed as queen; a decree is issued for all wives to honor their husbands.

2.title: King Xerxes seeks a new queen; young women are brought to the palace.
Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, is among them.
Esther wins favor and is crowned queen.
Mordecai uncovers a plot to assassinate the king; the plotters are executed.

3.title: Haman is promoted to the highest position under the king.
Mordecai refuses to bow to Haman; Haman becomes enraged.
Haman plans to destroy all Jews in the Persian Empire.
Haman convinces King Xerxes to issue a decree to annihilate the Jews.

4.title: Mordecai and the Jews mourn and fast upon hearing the decree.
Mordecai asks Esther to plead with the king on behalf of the Jews.
Mordecai tells Esther that she may have become queen for this very purpose.
Esther agrees to go to the king, risking her life, and asks for a fast.

5.title: Esther approaches the king; he extends his scepter, sparing her life.
Esther invites the king and Haman to a banquet.
Haman, still enraged by Mordecai, plans to have him hanged.

6.title: The king, unable to sleep, reads the chronicles and learns of Mordecai's loyalty.
Haman, thinking he will be honored, suggests a lavish parade, but it's for Mordecai.
Haman is forced to honor Mordecai publicly.

7.title: At the second banquet, Esther reveals her Jewish identity.
Esther exposes Haman's plot to destroy her people.
Haman is hanged on the very gallows he built for Mordecai.

8.title: Esther is given Haman's estate; Mordecai is promoted.
Esther pleads with the king to reverse Haman's decree.
A new decree allows the Jews to defend themselves against any attackers.
Jews rejoice, and many people in the empire support them.

9.title: The day of the planned massacre arrives; the Jews prevail over their enemies.
Mordecai sends letters instituting the Feast of Purim to commemorate their victory.

10.title: King Xerxes imposes tribute throughout his empire.
Mordecai becomes second in rank to the king, honored by the Jews for his work on their behalf.

11.title: An apocalyptic prologue: Mordecai dreams of two great dragons and a tiny stream that becomes a river — interpreted as the coming deliverance.

12.title: Mordecai overhears two royal eunuchs plotting against the king and reveals the conspiracy, earning the king's gratitude.

13.title: The full text of Haman's decree against the Jews is preserved, followed by Mordecai's earnest prayer for deliverance.

14.title: Esther humbles herself in fasting and prays at length for courage, confessing her revulsion at the trappings of pagan royalty.

15.title: Clothed in glory, Esther enters the king's presence, faints in fear, and is revived by his tender words — an expanded version of canonical Esther 5.

16.title: The full text of Artaxerxes' second decree, which condemns Haman as a Macedonian conspirator and confirms protection for the Jews.

1.title: Job is described as a blameless and upright man who fears God.
Satan challenges Job's righteousness, claiming it is due to his prosperity.
Job loses his oxen, donkeys, sheep, camels, and children in one day.
Job mourns deeply but worships God and does not sin.

2.title: Satan appears before God again; Job's integrity is questioned.
Job is afflicted with painful sores from head to toe.
Job's wife urges him to curse God and die; he refuses.
Job's three friends, Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar, come to comfort him.

3.title: Job curses the day of his birth, wishing he had never been born.
Job questions why he didn't die at birth and laments his suffering.

4.title: Eliphaz speaks, suggesting that Job's suffering is due to sin.

5.title: Eliphaz advises Job to accept God's discipline and repent.

6.title: Job expresses the depth of his anguish and defends his innocence.

7.title: Job speaks directly to God, lamenting his condition and seeking answers.

8.title: Bildad argues that God is just; Job's children must have sinned.
Bildad encourages Job to seek God, implying restoration if Job is righteous.

9.title: Job acknowledges God's power but questions how a man can be just before God.

10.title: Job laments his suffering and pleads with God for understanding.

11.title: Zophar rebukes Job, claiming his words are arrogant.
Zophar urges Job to repent and promises that his fortunes will be restored.

12.title: Job sarcastically responds, pointing out that his friends lack true wisdom.

13.title: Job wishes to argue his case directly with God.

14.title: Job reflects on the brevity and misery of life, asking if there is hope after death.

15.title: Eliphaz accuses Job of undermining religion and wisdom with his words.
Eliphaz describes the fate of the wicked, hinting Job's suffering is deserved.

16.title: Job laments his friends' lack of comfort and claims God has wronged him.

17.title: Job despairs, feeling his hope and strength are fading away.

18.title: Bildad describes the punishment of the wicked, indirectly accusing Job.

19.title: Job feels insulted by his friends and insists on his innocence.
Job declares his faith in a Redeemer who will stand on the earth.

20.title: Zophar describes the fleeting joy of the wicked and their inevitable downfall.

21.title: Job challenges the idea that the wicked always suffer and the righteous always prosper.

22.title: Eliphaz accuses Job of various sins and urges him to return to God.

23.title: Job desires to find God and present his case.

24.title: Job argues that the wicked often go unpunished in this life.

25.title: Bildad speaks briefly about God's greatness and human insignificance.

26.title: Job describes God's power and wisdom.

27.title: Job maintains his integrity and righteousness despite his suffering.

28.title: Job speaks of the value of wisdom, stating it is found only in the fear of the Lord.

29.title: Job reminisces about his past blessings and honor.

30.title: Job contrasts his former glory with his current suffering and humiliation.

31.title: Job declares his righteousness, listing his good deeds and challenging God to judge him.

32.title: Elihu, a younger man, becomes angry with Job and his friends for their arguments.
Elihu begins speaking, claiming to have wisdom from God.

33.title: Elihu challenges Job's claims of innocence and God's injustice.

34.title: Elihu argues that God is just and does not act wickedly.

35.title: Elihu contends that human righteousness does not affect God but impacts others.

36.title: Elihu describes God's greatness and uses suffering for discipline.

37.title: Elihu speaks of God's majesty, especially in creation and natural phenomena.

38.title: God answers Job out of a whirlwind, questioning him about the mysteries of creation.

39.title: God continues, asking Job to consider the wisdom in the natural world.

40.title: God challenges Job to answer; Job humbly admits his lack of understanding.
God describes the behemoth, demonstrating His power and wisdom.

41.title: God speaks of the leviathan, further displaying His might over creation.

42.title: Job repents, acknowledging God's sovereignty and his own ignorance.
God rebukes Job's friends for not speaking truthfully about Him.
God restores Job's fortunes, giving him twice as much as before.
Job is blessed with more children, wealth, and a long life.

1.title: The way of the righteous versus the way of the wicked.

2.title: The nations conspire against God, but His anointed King will reign.

3.title: David's plea for deliverance from his enemies; trust in God's protection.

8.title: God's majesty in creation and humanity's place in it.

16.title: A psalm of trust in God's protection and the joy of His presence.

19.title: The heavens declare God's glory; the law of the Lord is perfect.

22.title: A cry of despair that turns to praise, foreshadowing Christ's suffering.

23.title: The Lord is my Shepherd; a psalm of trust and comfort.

27.title: The Lord is my light and salvation; a psalm of confidence in God.

32.title: Blessed is the one whose sins are forgiven; a psalm of repentance.

34.title: David praises God for deliverance and encourages others to trust Him.

37.title: Do not fret over evildoers; trust in the Lord and do good.

40.title: A psalm of thanksgiving for God's help and a prayer for deliverance.

41.title: A prayer for mercy in times of illness and betrayal.

42.title: As a deer pants for water, so my soul longs for God.

46.title: God is our refuge and strength; a psalm of confidence in God's protection.

51.title: David's psalm of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba.

57.title: David seeks refuge in God amidst danger; a psalm of praise.

62.title: Find rest in God alone; a psalm of trust and confidence.

63.title: David thirsts for God in the wilderness; a psalm of longing and worship.

67.title: A prayer for God's blessing and for His ways to be known among the nations.

71.title: A prayer for God's help in old age and a declaration of His faithfulness.

72.title: A psalm of Solomon, praying for a righteous and prosperous reign.

73.title: The prosperity of the wicked contrasted with the reward of the righteous.

77.title: A cry to God in distress; remembering God's mighty deeds brings comfort.

84.title: How lovely is God's dwelling place; a longing to be in His presence.

86.title: A prayer of David for mercy, strength, and guidance.

88.title: A psalm of lament; a cry for help in deep distress.

89.title: A psalm praising God's faithfulness and lamenting the apparent failure of His promises.

90.title: A prayer of Moses, reflecting on God's eternity and human frailty.

91.title: Those who dwell in God's shelter find safety and refuge.

95.title: A call to worship and obedience to God, our Maker and Shepherd.

100.title: A psalm of thanksgiving; call to worship the Lord with gladness.

103.title: Bless the Lord, O my soul; a psalm of praise for God's mercy and grace.

104.title: A psalm celebrating God's creation and His care for all living things.

106.title: Praise for God's enduring love; a confession of Israel's rebellion and God's mercy.

107.title: Give thanks to the Lord for His steadfast love; recounting God's deliverance.

116.title: I love the Lord, for He heard my voice; a psalm of thanksgiving for answered prayer.

118.title: Give thanks to the Lord; His love endures forever; a messianic psalm of deliverance.

119.title: A lengthy meditation on the greatness of God's Word.

121.title: I lift up my eyes to the hills; a psalm of trust in God's protection.

127.title: Unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain.

130.title: Out of the depths I cry to You; a psalm of repentance and hope.

136.title: His love endures forever; a psalm of praise recounting God's deeds.

139.title: O Lord, You have searched me; a psalm about God's omniscience and omnipresence.

145.title: A psalm of praise declaring God's greatness and His goodness to all.

150.title: Praise the Lord; a final call to praise God with every instrument and breath.

1.title: Introduction to the Proverbs of Solomon; purpose of gaining wisdom and instruction.
Reverence for God is named the foundation of true understanding; rejecting correction marks the fool.
Warning against enticement by sinners.
Wisdom personified; calls out in the streets, warning against rejecting her counsel.

2.title: The benefits of seeking wisdom; protection from evil and understanding righteousness.
Wisdom enters the heart and leads to discernment and protection from wicked ways.

3.title: Encouragement to keep God's commandments and trust in Him for guidance.
A call to total reliance on God rather than human reasoning.
Honor the Lord with your wealth; promises of blessings and correction.
Blessed is the one who finds wisdom; its value exceeds silver and gold.

4.title: Advice to seek wisdom; wisdom leads to life and security.
The inner self is named the wellspring of conduct; it must be guarded above all else.

5.title: Warning against the seductive and destructive nature of adultery.
Encouragement to enjoy the wife of one's youth and be faithful in marriage.

6.title: Warnings against putting up security for others and being lazy.
Six things the Lord hates; seven that are detestable, including a lying tongue and a proud look.
Admonition to heed parents' instructions and avoid the adulterous woman.

7.title: A father's warning against the allure of the adulterous woman; a story of a young man led astray.

8.title: Wisdom calls out to all; describes her eternal nature and her role in creation.
Whoever finds wisdom finds life and receives favor from the Lord.

9.title: Wisdom has built her house; she invites all to come and learn.
Folly also calls out but leads to death; contrast between wisdom and folly.

10.title: A collection of Solomon's proverbs contrasting the righteous and the wicked.
Hatred stirs up conflict, but love covers all wrongs.

11.title: A false balance is an abomination to the Lord; contrast between the righteous and wicked.
Righteousness yields lasting good, and drawing others toward truth is named genuine wisdom.

12.title: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is stupid.
Anxiety weighs down the heart, but a kind word cheers it up.

13.title: A wise son heeds his father's instruction, but a mocker does not respond to rebukes.
Walk with the wise and become wise; a companion of fools suffers harm.

14.title: Wisdom and folly contrasted as a household-builder versus a household-wrecker.
A sober warning that paths that feel right can lead to ruin.

15.title: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Wisdom rooted in reverence; humility precedes any genuine honor.

16.title: Human planning is contrasted with the divine sovereignty that ultimately shapes our speech.
Commit to the Lord whatever you do, and He will establish your plans.
A warning that arrogance is the surest forerunner of ruin.

17.title: Modest peace is rated above abundant feasting accompanied by quarreling.
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity.

18.title: God's character itself is portrayed as a fortress where the upright find refuge.
Speech is portrayed as carrying weight enough to give life or to destroy.

19.title: Integrity in poverty is valued above wealth wedded to deceitful speech.
Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the Lord's purpose that prevails.

20.title: Wine is a mocker and beer a brawler; whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
The righteous lead blameless lives; blessed are their children after them.

21.title: A person may think their own ways are right, but the Lord weighs the heart.
The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but victory rests with the Lord.

22.title: Reputation is rated as the more durable inheritance than material wealth.
Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old, they will not turn from it.

23.title: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your own cleverness.
Don't envy those who prosper through wickedness; cultivate reverence instead.

24.title: If you falter in a time of trouble, how small is your strength!
Though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again, but the wicked stumble when calamity strikes.

25.title: Editorial note: this collection was assembled later by Hezekiah's scribes.
If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.

26.title: A collection of proverbs highlighting the behavior of fools and the consequences of folly.
Without wood a fire goes out; without a gossip, a quarrel dies down.

27.title: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

28.title: A contrast in moral courage: the guilty live in paranoia, the upright with confidence.
Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

29.title: Whoever remains stiff-necked after many rebukes will suddenly be destroyed—without remedy.
Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom's instruction.

30.title: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh, highlighting human limitation and the pursuit of wisdom.
Two things I ask of you, Lord; do not refuse me before I die: keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches.

31.title: A foreign king records the wisdom his mother instilled in him.
A wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies.

1.title: The book opens by identifying its author as a king of Jerusalem in David's line.
'Vanity of vanities,' says the Teacher; 'all is vanity.'
The repetitive cycles of nature illustrate the futility of human toil.
The Teacher explores the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge but finds it futile.

2.title: The Teacher tests pleasure, wealth, and accomplishments, but finds them meaningless.
Despite achieving greatness, the pursuit of pleasure and wisdom brings no lasting fulfillment.
The Teacher laments the futility of labor, knowing its results will be left to others.

3.title: There is a time for everything, a season for every activity under heaven.
The Teacher reflects on the purpose of life and the beauty in God's timing.
Observations of injustice in the world; God's judgment is emphasized.

4.title: The Teacher laments oppression and the loneliness of striving for success.
Two are better than one; the value of companionship and mutual support.
The futility of political power and the fickleness of popularity.

5.title: Admonition to approach God with reverence and sincerity.
Wealth does not satisfy; those who love money will never have enough.
Enjoyment of life is a gift from God, and true contentment comes from Him.

6.title: The Teacher reflects on the futility of wealth, honor, and unfulfilled desires.
All man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

7.title: A good name is better than precious ointment; reflections on wisdom and folly.
Consider the work of God; who can straighten what He has made crooked?
The Teacher seeks wisdom and meaning but acknowledges the limits of human understanding.

8.title: Wisdom gives insight; submission to authority is encouraged.
Recognizing the limitations of human understanding and the mystery of God's ways.
The Teacher observes the apparent injustice of life but trusts in God's ultimate judgment.

9.title: The righteous and the wise are in God's hands; reflections on death and life's uncertainties.
Encouragement to enjoy life and the blessings God provides.
Time and chance happen to all; the unpredictability of life is acknowledged.

10.title: A little folly can outweigh wisdom and honor; reflections on practical wisdom.
Various proverbs about wisdom, foolishness, and the unpredictability of life.

11.title: Cast your bread upon the waters; the benefits of generosity and taking risks.
Enjoy life in your youth but remember that God will bring everything to judgment.

12.title: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before difficult days come.
'Vanity of vanities,' says the Teacher; 'all is vanity.'
Solomon distills his entire search into a single charge: reverence and obedience to God.
Solomon closes by warning that nothing escapes final reckoning — hidden or open.

1.title: Introduction to the Song of Songs, attributed to Solomon.
The bride expresses her desire and love for the king, praising his love as better than wine.
The bride seeks her beloved, longing for his presence and companionship.
The king responds, praising the beauty of his beloved.

2.title: The bride pictures herself as a humble wildflower among the valleys.
The bride celebrates being publicly claimed and protected by her beloved.
The bride hears her beloved approaching; he invites her to come away with him.
A call to catch the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, symbolizing threats to their relationship.

3.title: The bride dreams of searching for her beloved in the city streets at night.
She finds him and brings him to her mother’s house, expressing deep affection.
A description of Solomon's procession, coming with splendor and royal guards.
Daughters of Jerusalem are called to witness King Solomon with his crown on his wedding day.

4.title: The king praises the beauty of his bride in detailed and poetic language.
He declares her beauty flawless and invites her to come with him.
The bride is described as a garden locked, a spring enclosed, a sealed fountain.
The bride invites her beloved to come into his garden and taste its choice fruits.

5.title: The beloved enters the garden; the joy of intimacy is expressed.
The bride dreams that her beloved knocks, but she hesitates to open.
She searches for him but does not find him; she is beaten by the city guards.
She describes her beloved as radiant and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

6.title: The daughters of Jerusalem ask where the beloved has gone; they seek him together.
The king praises his bride, comparing her beauty to the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem.
A description of the bride as beautiful and awe-inspiring as the dawn.

7.title: The king continues to praise the physical beauty of his bride from head to toe.
The bride's beauty captivates the king, and he expresses his deep affection for her.
The bride declares her belonging to her beloved and his desire for her.
She invites him to go out to the countryside with her, expressing her love and desire.

8.title: The bride wishes for open affection, free from societal restrictions.
The bride speaks of love as strong as death, its jealousy as unyielding as the grave.
The bride's brothers speak of their protective role; a dialogue on love and maturity.
The king and the bride express mutual longing; the song ends with a call to come away.

1.title: Introduction to Isaiah's vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
God's indictment against Judah for their rebellion and corruption.
A call for repentance: 'Wash and make yourselves clean.'
'Come now, let us reason together,' says the Lord; a call for forgiveness and renewal.

2.title: A vision of the future: the mountain of the Lord's temple will be established.
A prophecy of peace: nations will beat their swords into plowshares.
God's judgment against pride and idolatry.

3.title: Judgment against Jerusalem for their leaders' corruption and people's arrogance.
Condemnation of the daughters of Zion for their pride and vanity.

4.title: A prophecy of the Branch of the Lord, a symbol of beauty and glory for the remnant of Israel.
God's protective presence over His people in the future kingdom.

5.title: The song of the vineyard: a parable of Israel's unfaithfulness.
Woes pronounced on those who exploit others and live in luxury without regard for God.
A prophecy of judgment coming from distant nations.

6.title: Isaiah's vision of the Lord seated on His throne, high and exalted.
Isaiah's confession of sinfulness and the purification of his lips by a seraph.
God's call: 'Whom shall I send?' Isaiah responds, 'Here am I. Send me!'

7.title: The Syro-Ephraimite war; Ahaz fears the coalition against Judah.
The prophecy of the virgin birth of Immanuel, meaning 'God with us.'

8.title: The coming invasion of Assyria as a judgment against Israel and Judah.
Fear the Lord, not man; trust in Him as a sanctuary.

9.title: A prophecy of light shining in Galilee, dispelling darkness.
'For unto us a child is born,' a prophecy of the Messiah, the Prince of Peace.
Judgment against the northern kingdom of Israel for its pride and wickedness.

10.title: Woe to those who enact unjust laws and oppress the people.
Assyria is described as God's instrument of judgment but will itself be judged.
A remnant of Israel will return to the mighty God.

11.title: A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; a prophecy of the Messiah's reign.
The peaceable kingdom: the wolf will live with the lamb.

12.title: Songs of praise and thanksgiving for God's salvation.

13.title: Prophecies against Babylon and other nations, pronouncing judgment for their sins.

17.title: An oracle concerning Damascus and Israel's downfall.

19.title: A prophecy of Egypt's judgment and future blessing.

24.title: A vision of the earth's devastation; judgment on all the earth.
A remnant will raise their voices and give glory to the Lord.

25.title: Praise for God's deliverance and the promise of a feast for all peoples.
Death itself is named God's final enemy, destined for permanent defeat alongside grief.

26.title: A song of praise for God's salvation and the strong city.
'You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in you.'

27.title: God will punish Leviathan, the fleeing serpent.
Israel will blossom and fill the earth with fruit.

28.title: Woe to the leaders of Ephraim and Judah; warnings against complacency and pride.

30.title: Woe to the obstinate children who rely on Egypt instead of God.

35.title: The future glory of Zion; the desert will bloom and rejoice.

36.title: Assyrian invasion; Sennacherib's threats against Jerusalem.

37.title: Hezekiah seeks God's help; God delivers Jerusalem from Assyria.

38.title: Hezekiah's illness and recovery; the sign of the sun moving backward.

39.title: Envoys from Babylon visit Hezekiah; prophecy of Babylonian exile.

40.title: The pivotal turn of the book: God commissions a message of comfort to the exiles.
'Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength.'

42.title: The Servant of the Lord; a prophecy of the Messiah bringing justice.

53.title: The suffering Servant; a prophecy of Christ's atoning death.

56.title: Salvation for all nations; a call for righteousness and justice.

60.title: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come,' a prophecy of Zion's future glory.

61.title: 'The Spirit of the Sovereign Lord is on me,' a prophecy of the Messiah's ministry.

65.title: The promise of a new heaven and a new earth.

66.title: God's final judgment and gathering of all nations; a new order established.

1.title: Introduction to Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, a prophet in Judah.
God calls Jeremiah as a prophet to the nations, even before he was born.
God touches Jeremiah's mouth and gives him His words to speak.
The visions of the almond tree and boiling pot symbolize coming judgment.

2.title: God recounts Israel's early devotion and accuses them of forsaking Him for idols.
Israel has committed two sins: forsaking God and digging broken cisterns.
Israel's wickedness and backsliding will bring about their own punishment.

3.title: God calls Israel an unfaithful wife but invites her to return and repent.
A promise of mercy and restoration if Israel returns to God.
Call for backsliding children to return; God promises healing.

4.title: God calls for Israel's repentance and warns of impending disaster from the north.
Jeremiah's anguish over the coming destruction of Jerusalem.

5.title: Jerusalem's inhabitants are corrupt and unrepentant.
Despite their rebellion, God will not completely destroy them.

6.title: Warning of an imminent invasion; Jerusalem is compared to a woman in labor.
God calls Israel to return to the ancient paths of righteousness.

7.title: Jeremiah stands at the temple gate, proclaiming God's judgment on false worship.
God instructs Jeremiah not to pray for the people because of their persistent idolatry.

8.title: Jeremiah laments over Israel's stubborn refusal to repent and their impending punishment.
The harvest is past, the summer has ended, and we are not saved.

9.title: Jeremiah weeps for his people and their coming destruction.
Let not the wise boast of their wisdom but boast in knowing the Lord.

10.title: God's condemnation of idolatry; idols are worthless compared to the living God.
Jeremiah acknowledges that a person's way is not in themselves; seeks correction from God.

11.title: God's people have broken the covenant; judgment is pronounced against them.
Jeremiah learns of a plot against his life by the people of Anathoth.

12.title: Jeremiah questions God's justice; God assures that greater challenges are to come.
A promise of restoration for those who turn to God, including Israel's neighbors.

13.title: A parable of the linen belt symbolizes Judah's pride and corruption.
A call to repent before it is too late; warning of captivity and exile.

14.title: A severe drought in Judah; Jeremiah intercedes for the people.
God's rejection of false prophets and their deceptive messages of peace.

15.title: Even Moses and Samuel could not intercede for this rebellious generation.
Jeremiah pleads for vindication and complains of his loneliness and suffering.

16.title: God commands Jeremiah not to marry or have children as a sign of coming judgment.
A prophecy of the nations coming to recognize Israel's God in the end times.

17.title: Judah's sin is engraved with an iron stylus; only God can heal.
Cursed is the one who trusts in man; blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord.
The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure; who can understand it?

18.title: The potter's house: a metaphor of God's sovereignty over Israel.
God can change His plans for a nation based on their repentance or rebellion.
Jeremiah faces plots against his life by his own people.

19.title: Jeremiah smashes a clay jar as a symbol of God's coming judgment on Jerusalem.
God will smash Jerusalem and its people as one breaks a potter's jar.

20.title: Jeremiah is persecuted by Pashhur the priest and is put in stocks.
Jeremiah's complaint: he is ridiculed and feels deceived by God but cannot stop prophesying.

21.title: King Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah for counsel; Jeremiah prophesies destruction.
The way of life and the way of death: surrender to Babylon and live, resist and perish.

22.title: God commands justice and righteousness; judgment against King Jehoiakim and others.
Coniah (Jehoiachin) is rejected as king; none of his descendants will sit on David's throne.

23.title: Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter God's flock.
The prophecy of the Righteous Branch, a king from David's line who will reign wisely.
God denounces false prophets who deceive the people with their lies.

24.title: The vision of two baskets of figs: good figs representing the exiles who will be restored, bad figs symbolizing those who remain and are destroyed.

25.title: Jeremiah's prophecy of 70 years of captivity in Babylon.
The cup of God's wrath to be drunk by all nations, starting with Jerusalem.

26.title: Jeremiah prophesies at the temple; he is seized and threatened with death.
Jeremiah is spared after elders recall Micah's prophecy and Hezekiah's response.

27.title: Jeremiah wears a yoke to symbolize Judah's submission to Babylon.
Warning against false prophets who predict peace.

28.title: Hananiah falsely predicts the end of Babylonian domination; Jeremiah rebukes him.
Hananiah dies as Jeremiah prophesied, confirming his words were false.

29.title: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles in Babylon, encouraging them to seek peace and prosperity.
'For I know the plans I have for you,' declares the Lord, 'plans to prosper you and not to harm you.'

30.title: God promises the restoration of Israel and Judah from captivity and healing.
The city will be rebuilt, and the people will be restored to the land.

31.title: A prophecy of hope for Israel's restoration and the new covenant God will make.
'I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.'

32.title: Jeremiah buys a field as a sign of future hope, even as Jerusalem is besieged.
Jeremiah's prayer acknowledges God's power and justice.

33.title: God promises restoration and a future Davidic ruler.
The righteous Branch from David's line will execute justice and righteousness.

34.title: Jeremiah warns King Zedekiah of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon.
The people break their covenant of freeing slaves; judgment is pronounced.

35.title: The Recabites are commended for their obedience to their forefather's command.
Their example of obedience is contrasted with Judah's disobedience.

36.title: Jeremiah dictates God's words to Baruch; King Jehoiakim burns the scroll.
The scroll is rewritten with additional prophecies of judgment.

37.title: Jeremiah prophesies against Zedekiah; he is imprisoned for being accused of deserting.
Jeremiah is kept in the court of the guard and given bread.

38.title: Jeremiah is thrown into a cistern but is later rescued by Ebed-Melech.
Zedekiah secretly consults Jeremiah, who urges him to surrender to Babylon.

39.title: Jerusalem falls to Babylon; Zedekiah is captured, and the city is burned.
Nebuchadnezzar spares Jeremiah and gives him the option to go to Babylon or stay in Judah.

40.title: Jeremiah is released and chooses to stay with the remnant in Judah.
Gedaliah is appointed governor; a remnant gathers under him.

41.title: Ishmael assassinates Gedaliah and kills many people; violence ensues in Mizpah.
Johanan pursues Ishmael to rescue captives and plans to flee to Egypt.

42.title: The remnant seeks Jeremiah's counsel; he warns against fleeing to Egypt.
God's clear command: do not go to Egypt, or disaster will follow.

43.title: Despite Jeremiah's warning, the remnant goes to Egypt, taking him along.
Jeremiah prophesies Nebuchadnezzar's conquest of Egypt.

44.title: Jeremiah condemns the people's idolatry in Egypt and warns of judgment.
The people reject Jeremiah's message and continue their idol worship.

45.title: God's promise to Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, in the midst of judgment.

46.title: Judgment against Egypt, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Elam, and Babylon.

50.title: A prophecy against Babylon, foretelling its destruction and Israel's restoration.

52.title: A summary of Jerusalem's fall, Zedekiah's capture, and the destruction of the temple.
Jehoiachin is released from prison in Babylon and shown kindness by the king.

1.title: Jerusalem lies desolate; she who was once great among the nations is now like a widow.
Her foes have become her masters; the Lord has brought her grief because of her many sins.
The city's suffering is unparalleled; she calls for passersby to consider her sorrow.

2.title: The Lord has covered Daughter Zion with the cloud of His anger; He has hurled down the splendor of Israel.
God has laid waste His dwelling; He has destroyed His appointed meeting place.
The prophet's eyes fail from weeping; children and infants faint in the streets.

3.title: The prophet speaks of personal affliction under God's wrath.
He remembers his affliction and his soul is downcast.
Yet, he proclaims, 'Because of the Lord's great love we are not consumed; His compassions never fail.'
The Lord is good to those whose hope is in Him, to the one who seeks Him.
Though He brings grief, He will show compassion; He does not willingly afflict or grieve anyone.

4.title: Gold has lost its luster; sacred gems are scattered at every street corner.
Children beg for food, but no one gives them anything.
Compassionate women have cooked their own children; the siege has brought extreme desperation.

5.title: The community pleads with the Lord to remember what has happened to them.
Our ancestors sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment.
Despite everything, 'You, Lord, reign forever; your throne endures from generation to generation.'
'Restore us to yourself, Lord, that we may return; renew our days as of old.'

1.title: Ezekiel, a priest in exile, has a vision by the Kebar River.
He sees a stormy wind, bright lights, and four living creatures with unique appearances.
Wheels within wheels beside the creatures, full of eyes; a representation of God's omnipresence.
Above the expanse is a throne, and on it a figure like a man; Ezekiel beholds the glory of the Lord.

2.title: God speaks to Ezekiel, calling him 'son of man' and sending him to the rebellious house of Israel.
God warns Ezekiel not to fear the people's reactions.
Ezekiel is instructed to eat a scroll containing words of lament and woe.

3.title: Ezekiel eats the scroll; it tastes as sweet as honey.
God sends Ezekiel to speak His words to Israel.
Ezekiel is appointed as a watchman to warn the people.
God makes Ezekiel's tongue stick to the roof of his mouth; he will only speak when God opens his mouth.

4.title: Ezekiel enacts a symbolic siege of Jerusalem using a clay tablet.
He lies on his side for 390 days for Israel's sin and 40 days for Judah's sin.
He is instructed to eat measured, sparse rations symbolizing famine during the siege.

5.title: Ezekiel cuts his hair and divides it, symbolizing the fate of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
A third will die by plague, a third by the sword, and a third will be scattered.

6.title: Ezekiel prophesies against Israel's mountains, denouncing idolatry.
A remnant will survive and remember the Lord among the nations.

7.title: A message of doom: 'The end has come upon the four corners of the land.'
Their silver and gold will not save them in the day of God's wrath.

8.title: Ezekiel is transported in a vision to Jerusalem.
He sees various abominations and idolatry committed in the temple.
Women weeping for Tammuz; men worshiping the sun.

9.title: God calls for those appointed to execute judgment on Jerusalem.
A man with a writing kit marks those who grieve over sin; the rest are slain.

10.title: Ezekiel sees the glory of God departing from the temple.
The cherubim lift their wings, and the glory of the Lord moves away from the threshold.

11.title: Leaders are condemned for giving wicked counsel.
God promises to be a sanctuary for exiles.
A promise of a new heart and spirit; removal of the heart of stone.

12.title: Ezekiel acts out going into exile, digging through the wall.
This sign predicts the exile of the prince (Zedekiah) and the people of Jerusalem.
God refutes the proverb that visions fail; His words will be fulfilled without delay.

13.title: Condemnation of false prophets who deceive the people with false visions.
They whitewash flimsy walls; their work will be destroyed.

14.title: Elders inquire of Ezekiel; God exposes their idolatry.
Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in the land, they could only save themselves by their righteousness.

15.title: Jerusalem is compared to a useless vine, good only for fuel.
God will set His face against them; they will know He is the Lord when He sets the land desolate.

16.title: An allegory of Jerusalem as an unfaithful wife; God recounts His care and her infidelity.
Jerusalem's harlotry with other nations and idols is condemned.
Despite their unfaithfulness, God promises to remember His covenant and establish an everlasting covenant.

17.title: A parable of two eagles and a vine representing Babylon, Egypt, and Judah's kings.
God will plant a tender sprig on a high mountain, symbolizing the Messiah's kingdom.

18.title: God rejects the proverb 'The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
Every soul belongs to God; the soul who sins shall die.
If the wicked turn from their sins, they will live; God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked.

19.title: A lamentation for the princes of Israel depicted as lions and a withered vine.

20.title: Elders inquire of Ezekiel; God recounts Israel's history of rebellion.
God promises to gather Israel but also to purge the rebels.

21.title: A prophecy of God's sword drawn against Jerusalem.
The king of Babylon stands at the crossroads, choosing to attack Jerusalem.

22.title: Jerusalem is accused of bloodshed and idolatry.
God sought someone to stand in the gap but found no one.

23.title: An allegory of two sisters, representing Samaria (Oholah) and Jerusalem (Oholibah), and their unfaithfulness.
Both sisters are judged for their adulteries and bloodshed.

24.title: The parable of the rusty cooking pot symbolizes Jerusalem's impurities.
God tells Ezekiel his wife will die, and he must not mourn publicly.
Ezekiel is a sign to the people; they will do as he has done when Jerusalem falls.

25.title: Judgment against Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia for their actions against Israel.

26.title: Prophecy against Tyre; it will be destroyed and become a bare rock.

28.title: Condemnation of the prince of Tyre for his pride, claiming to be a god.
A lament over the king of Tyre, depicting his fall from perfection.

29.title: Judgment against Egypt; it will be desolate for forty years.

31.title: Assyria compared to a cedar of Lebanon; its fall serves as a warning to Egypt.

32.title: A lament over Pharaoh and Egypt; they will descend to the realm of the dead.

33.title: God reiterates Ezekiel's role as a watchman for Israel.
God assures that He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked; calls for repentance.
A survivor reports Jerusalem's fall; Ezekiel's mouth is opened.

34.title: God condemns the shepherds (leaders) for neglecting the flock.
God Himself will search for His sheep and look after them.
The Messianic shepherd promise: God will install a new David to lead his people.

35.title: Judgment against Edom (Mount Seir) for its hostility toward Israel.

36.title: Prophecy to the mountains of Israel; they will produce fruit for God's people.
God will restore Israel for the sake of His holy name.
Promise of a new heart and a new spirit; God will put His Spirit within them.

37.title: Ezekiel sees a valley of dry bones; God commands him to prophesy to them.
The bones come to life, symbolizing the restoration of Israel.
The prophecy of two sticks representing Judah and Israel reuniting as one nation.

38.title: Prophecy against Gog of the land of Magog; a future invasion of Israel.
God's fury will be unleashed; Gog's armies will be defeated.

39.title: God's glory among the nations; Israel will know that He is the Lord.

40.title: In the 25th year of exile, Ezekiel is given a vision of a new temple.
Detailed measurements of the temple's structures are provided.

43.title: The glory of the Lord returns to the temple from the east.

44.title: Instructions regarding the priests and their duties in the new temple.

47.title: Ezekiel sees water flowing from the temple, bringing life wherever it goes.
Boundaries of the restored land are described; division among the tribes.

48.title: The name of the city from that time on will be 'The Lord Is There' (Yahweh Shammah).

1.title: Daniel and his three friends are taken captive to Babylon during King Nebuchadnezzar's reign.
Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food; requests vegetables and water.
God gives them knowledge and understanding; Daniel can interpret visions and dreams.

2.title: King Nebuchadnezzar has a troubling dream; demands interpretation without revealing the dream.
Daniel and his friends pray for mercy to reveal the mystery.
God reveals the dream and its interpretation to Daniel in a vision.
Daniel describes the dream of a great statue made of various metals.
Daniel interprets the dream, prophesying successive kingdoms and God's eternal kingdom.
Nebuchadnezzar honors Daniel and promotes him and his friends.

3.title: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden image; commands all to worship it.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship the image.
They are thrown into a fiery furnace heated seven times hotter.
A fourth figure appears with them in the fire; they are unharmed.
Nebuchadnezzar praises God and promotes them in the province of Babylon.

4.title: Nebuchadnezzar recounts his dream of a great tree that is cut down.
Daniel interprets the dream, predicting Nebuchadnezzar's downfall due to pride.
The prophecy is fulfilled; Nebuchadnezzar loses his sanity and lives like an animal.
Nebuchadnezzar's sanity is restored after he acknowledges God's sovereignty.

5.title: King Belshazzar holds a great feast using sacred vessels from the temple.
A hand writes mysterious words on the wall.
Daniel is brought in to interpret the writing.
The message reads 'Mene, Mene, Tekel, Parsin'; Daniel interprets it as God's judgment.
That very night, Belshazzar is killed; Darius the Mede takes over the kingdom.

6.title: Darius appoints administrators, including Daniel, who excels above others.
Jealous officials trick the king into issuing a decree against prayer to any but the king.
Daniel continues praying to God three times a day.
Daniel is thrown into the lions' den; the king hopes for his deliverance.
God sends an angel to shut the lions' mouths; Daniel is unharmed.
Daniel is lifted out; his accusers are thrown in and killed by the lions.
Darius issues a decree honoring the God of Daniel.

7.title: Daniel has a vision of four great beasts coming out of the sea.
He sees the Ancient of Days on the throne; judgment is set.
One like a son of man approaches the Ancient of Days; receives everlasting dominion.
Daniel is troubled; an angel explains the vision as representing kingdoms and the saints' victory.

8.title: Daniel has a vision of a ram with two horns and a goat with a prominent horn.
Gabriel interprets the vision, explaining it refers to future kingdoms (Media-Persia and Greece).
A fierce king will arise, but will be destroyed by divine power.

9.title: Daniel understands from Jeremiah's writings that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
He prays with fasting and confession for his people.
Gabriel appears to give Daniel insight.
Prophecy of the seventy 'sevens' to bring in righteousness and anoint the Most Holy.

10.title: Daniel receives a revelation during the reign of Cyrus; mourns for three weeks.
He sees a man clothed in linen with a glorious appearance.
The angel tells Daniel he was delayed by the prince of Persia; Michael helped him.
The vision concerns future events for Daniel's people.

11.title: A detailed prophecy of future conflicts between the kings of the North and South.
A contemptible person arises, seizes the kingdom through intrigue.
The abomination that causes desolation is set up.
A king will exalt himself above every god; acts as he pleases.

12.title: Michael will arise; a time of distress like no other; deliverance for those written in the book.
An early Old Testament prophecy of bodily resurrection and final judgment.
Daniel is told to seal the words until the time of the end.
Daniel is assured he will rise to receive his allotted inheritance at the end of days.

1.title: Hosea's ministry placed across the long reigns of five kings spanning both kingdoms.
God commands Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, symbolizing Israel's unfaithfulness to God.
Hosea's children are given symbolic names: Jezreel (God will scatter), Lo-Ruhamah (No mercy), and Lo-Ammi (Not my people).

2.title: God brings charges against Israel for her unfaithfulness and idolatry.
God will block Israel's way to lead her back to Him.
Despite Israel's unfaithfulness, God promises to allure her back and restore the covenant.
God will show love to 'No mercy' and say to 'Not my people,' 'You are my people.'

3.title: God instructs Hosea to love Gomer again, symbolizing God's love for Israel despite her idolatry.
Hosea buys Gomer back and renews his commitment to her.
A prophecy that Israel will be without king or sacrifice for a time but will return to seek the Lord.

4.title: God's lawsuit against Israel: no faithfulness, love, or acknowledgment of God in the land.
'My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge'; priests and people have rejected God's law.
Idolatry and immorality have led the people astray.

5.title: Judgment is pronounced on priests, people, and leaders for their sins.
Their deeds do not permit them to return to God; a spirit of prostitution is in their heart.
God will withdraw until they acknowledge their guilt and seek His face.

6.title: 'Come, let us return to the Lord'; a call for repentance and restoration.
God laments Israel's fleeting loyalty; 'Your love is like the morning mist.'
God prefers heart-loyalty to ritual sacrifice — the line Jesus would later quote.

7.title: God desires to heal Israel, but their sins are exposed.
Ephraim mixes with the nations; Israel is like a flat cake not turned over.
They do not cry out to God from their hearts but wail on their beds.

8.title: An eagle is over the house of the Lord because they have broken the covenant.
'They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind'; their alliances and idols will not save them.
Both kingdoms have replaced God with their own construction projects; fire is announced.

9.title: Israel is told not to rejoice like other nations; they have been unfaithful to God.
The days of punishment have come; Israel knows it.
God's verdict: dispersion among foreign nations as the consequence of disobedience.

10.title: Israel is a luxuriant vine that yields fruit for itself; the more they prospered, the more they built idols.
'Sow righteousness for yourselves, reap the fruit of unfailing love.'
But they have planted wickedness and reaped evil; trusted in their own strength.

11.title: God recalls Israel's adoption as a beloved child; the Exodus framed as a father's rescue.
The more God called, the more they went away; they sacrificed to Baals.
God's compassion is aroused; He struggles with the decision to punish Israel.

12.title: Ephraim feeds on the wind; pursues alliances with Assyria and Egypt.
Return to God; maintain love and justice, and wait for Him always.
God spoke to the prophets and gave many visions to guide Israel.

13.title: When Ephraim spoke, people trembled; but they became guilty of Baal worship and died.
'I have been the Lord your God ever since Egypt; you shall acknowledge no God but me.'
God questions whether to ransom them from death but concludes judgment is necessary.

14.title: A final call to Israel: 'Return, Israel, to the Lord your God.'
God promises to heal their waywardness and love them freely.
'Who is wise? Let them realize these things'; the ways of the Lord are right.

1.title: Introduction to Joel, son of Pethuel.
A call to elders and inhabitants to hear about an unprecedented disaster.
Description of a devastating locust plague consuming the land.
Priests are urged to mourn; a call for fasting and assembly.
'Alas for the day! For the day of the Lord is near'; a warning of impending judgment.

2.title: Sound the trumpet; the day of the Lord is coming, a day of darkness and gloom.
A call to return to the Lord with all one's heart, with fasting and weeping.
The turning point: God responds to national repentance with renewed favor.
'I will restore to you the years that the locust has eaten.'
'I will pour out my Spirit on all people'; prophecy of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

3.title: In those days, God will restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem.
God will gather all nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment.
Proclaim war among the nations; prepare for battle.
The Lord will roar from Zion; God will be a refuge for His people.
Promise of abundant blessings; mountains will drip new wine.

1.title: Introduction to Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa during the reigns of Uzziah and Jeroboam II.
God pronounces judgment on Damascus for its transgressions.
Judgment against Gaza for taking captive whole communities.
Judgment against Tyre for violating a treaty of brotherhood.
Judgment against Edom for pursuing his brother with a sword.

2.title: Judgment against Moab for desecrating the bones of Edom's king.
Judgment against Judah for rejecting God's law.
Judgment against Israel for oppressing the righteous and the poor.
Israel is condemned for corrupting the Nazarites and commanding prophets not to prophesy.

3.title: Israel is called to hear God's word against them.
'You only have I chosen of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you.'
God reveals His plans to His prophets before acting.
A remnant will be saved, like a shepherd rescues pieces from a lion's mouth.

4.title: Condemnation of the 'cows of Bashan' who oppress the poor.
God recounts sending hardships, yet Israel did not return to Him.
'Prepare to meet your God, O Israel.'

5.title: 'Seek me and live'; a call to seek the Lord instead of idols.
'Seek good, not evil, that you may live.'
God rejects Israel's feasts and offerings due to their injustice.
'Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!'

6.title: Woe to those at ease in Zion, feeling secure but ignoring impending disaster.
Condemnation of those indulging in luxury while neglecting the ruin of Joseph (Israel).
God abhors Israel's pride; He will deliver up the city.

7.title: Amos sees visions of locusts and fire; he intercedes, and God relents.
Vision of a plumb line; God will no longer spare Israel.
Amaziah the priest opposes Amos; Amos defends his prophetic calling.

8.title: Vision of ripe fruit symbolizing the end is near for Israel.
'The days are coming,' declares the Lord, 'when I will send a famine... of hearing the words of the Lord.'

9.title: God stands by the altar, commanding the destruction of the sanctuary.
Despite destruction, God will not totally destroy the house of Jacob.
Promise of restoring David's fallen tent and repairing its ruins.
A prophecy of abundant blessings and restoration of the land.

1.title: The vision of Obadiah concerning Edom; God announces judgment.
Edom's pride has deceived them; they dwell in the clefts of the rocks.
Because of violence against Jacob, shame will cover Edom.
Edom is warned not to gloat over Judah's misfortune.
'The day of the Lord is near for all nations'; as you have done, it will be done to you.
Mount Zion is preserved as a place of refuge while Edom is judged.
Saviors will ascend Mount Zion to govern the mountains of Esau; the kingdom will be the Lord's.
The word of the Lord comes to Jonah to go to Nineveh and preach against it.
Jonah flees in the opposite direction to Tarshish by ship.
God sends a great storm; sailors are afraid, and Jonah is asleep.
Jonah admits he is the cause; tells sailors to throw him into the sea.
They throw Jonah overboard; the sea becomes calm.

2.title: Jonah prays to God from inside the fish.
He acknowledges God's deliverance: 'You brought my life up from the pit.'
The Lord commands the fish, and it vomits Jonah onto dry land.

3.title: After his rescue from the sea, Jonah is given his original commission a second time.
Jonah proclaims, 'Forty more days and Nineveh will be overthrown.'
The Ninevites believe God; they declare a fast and put on sackcloth.
God sees their repentance and spares the city from destruction.

4.title: Jonah is displeased and angry that God spared Nineveh.
He acknowledges God's gracious and compassionate nature.
God provides a plant to give Jonah shade, which pleases him.
God sends a worm to wither the plant; Jonah becomes faint.
God teaches Jonah a lesson about compassion for Nineveh's inhabitants.

1.title: Introduction to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
God is coming to witness against the people for their transgressions.
Samaria will become a heap of rubble; idols destroyed.

2.title: Woe to those who plan iniquity and oppress others.
False prophets tell Micah not to prophesy about such things.
A promise to gather the remnant of Israel like sheep in a pen.

3.title: Micah rebukes the leaders for injustice and corruption.
False prophets lead people astray for personal gain.
Micah is filled with power and the Spirit to declare Israel's sin.
Because of their sins, Zion will be plowed like a field.

4.title: In the last days, the mountain of the Lord's temple will be established.
Nations will beat swords into plowshares; peace will prevail.
God will gather the lame and outcasts; the Lord will reign over them.

5.title: 'But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though small, out of you will come a ruler over Israel.'
He will shepherd His flock in the strength of the Lord.
God will remove reliance on military might and destroy idols.

6.title: God brings a lawsuit against Israel; calls the mountains to hear.
What does the Lord require? Sacrifices are not enough.
'He has shown you what is good: to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God.'
Because of sin, God will make them ill and desolate.

7.title: The faithful have vanished; there is much corruption.
Micah resolves to watch in hope for the Lord; God will hear him.
Though I have fallen, I will rise; the Lord will be my light.
God pardons sin and delights to show mercy.
God will be faithful to Jacob and show love to Abraham, as promised.

1.title: Opening of an oracle of judgment against the imperial capital of Assyria.
The Lord is a jealous and avenging God; He takes vengeance on His foes.
'The Lord is good, a refuge in times of trouble'; He cares for those who trust in Him.
With an overwhelming flood, He will make an end of Nineveh.

2.title: An attacker advances against Nineveh; guard the fortress.
Shields of soldiers are red; warriors clad in scarlet.
Nineveh is like a pool whose water is draining away.
'I am against you,' declares the Lord Almighty; the young lions will be devoured.

3.title: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder.
'I am against you,' declares the Lord; He will lift up your skirts over your face.
All who see you will flee; Nineveh is in ruins.
Nothing can heal your wound; everyone who hears the news claps their hands at your fall.

1.title: The prophecy that Habakkuk the prophet received.
Habakkuk asks God how long he must call for help without an answer.
God replies that He is raising up the Babylonians to execute judgment.
Habakkuk questions why God would use a wicked nation to judge Judah.

2.title: Habakkuk resolves to stand at his watch and wait for God's reply.
The Lord tells him to write down the revelation and make it plain.
'The righteous will live by his faith'; contrasts the proud and the upright.
Five woes pronounced against the arrogant, violent, and idolatrous.
'The earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord.'

3.title: The book closes with a psalm — Habakkuk's prayer set for liturgical use.
He pleads with God to renew His deeds in their time.
Though the fig tree does not bud and fields yield no food, yet I will rejoice in the Lord.
'The Sovereign Lord is my strength'; He enables me to tread on the heights.

1.title: Introduction to Zephaniah during the reign of Josiah.
God declares He will sweep away everything from the face of the earth.
Judgment against Judah for idolatry and turning away from the Lord.
'The great day of the Lord is near'; a day of wrath and distress.

2.title: Call to gather together and seek the Lord before the day of wrath.
Judgment pronounced against Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush, and Assyria.
Nineveh will become desolate, the city once full of pride.

3.title: Woe to the city of oppressors, rebellious and defiled.
The Lord within her is righteous; He does no wrong.
God declares He will pour out His wrath but then restore the nations.
Promise to purify the lips of the peoples so they may call on the Lord.
'The Lord your God is with you, the Mighty Warrior who saves'; He will rejoice over you with singing.

1.title: Haggai speaks to Zerubbabel and Joshua during the second year of King Darius.
The people say it is not time to rebuild the Lord's house.
God asks if it is right for them to live in paneled houses while His house remains in ruins.
God urges them to consider their ways and rebuild the temple.
Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the remnant obey the Lord and begin work.

2.title: Haggai encourages the leaders and people to be strong and work.
God will shake the heavens and the earth, and the desired of all nations will come.
God promises the rebuilt temple will surpass Solomon's in glory.
A lesson on holiness and defilement; the people's disobedience affected their offerings.
God promises to overthrow thrones and make Zerubbabel His signet ring.

1.title: Introduction to Zechariah during the second year of Darius.
'Return to me,' declares the Lord Almighty, 'and I will return to you.'
Vision of a man among myrtle trees; angelic messengers report peace in the land.
God declares He will return to Jerusalem with mercy; the temple will be rebuilt.

2.title: Vision of a man measuring Jerusalem; the city will be without walls.
'I myself will be a wall of fire around it,' declares the Lord.
God calls Zion to rejoice; many nations will be joined with the Lord.

3.title: A heavenly courtroom scene: the high priest stands accused while the angel intervenes.
Joshua's filthy garments are removed; he is given clean clothes, symbolizing the removal of sin.
The Branch (Messiah) is promised; God will remove the sin of the land in a single day.

4.title: Vision of a gold lampstand and two olive trees.
'Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty.
Do not despise the day of small things; Zerubbabel will complete the temple.

5.title: Vision of a flying scroll representing the curse over the whole land.
Vision of a woman in a basket symbolizing wickedness being removed from the land.

6.title: Vision of four chariots representing the four spirits of heaven.
Crowning of Joshua the high priest, symbolizing the coming Branch who will build the temple.

7.title: Question about continuing fasts during the fifth month.
God desires true justice, mercy, and compassion; not ritual fasting.

8.title: 'I will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem.'
God will save His people from the east and west and bring them back.
Speak truth, render true judgments, and promote peace.

9.title: 'Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Your king comes to you... gentle and riding on a donkey.'
The Lord will save His people like a flock; they will sparkle in His land.

11.title: Zechariah enacts the role of a shepherd; rejection leads to the breaking of covenants.

12.title: God will pour out a spirit of grace; they will mourn for the one they pierced.

13.title: A fountain will be opened to cleanse from sin and impurity.

14.title: On that day, the Lord's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives; the day of the Lord comes.
Final eschatological vision: God's universal kingship over the renewed earth.

1.title: Opening of the final Old Testament prophetic book, attributed to Malachi.
'I have loved you,' says the Lord. But you ask, 'How have you loved us?'
God rebukes the priests for showing contempt by offering blemished sacrifices.
'My name will be great among the nations,' says the Lord Almighty.

2.title: Warning to the priests to honor God's name or face a curse.
Condemnation of unfaithfulness; men divorcing their wives and marrying foreign women.
The people weary God with their words, questioning His justice.

3.title: 'I will send my messenger, who will prepare the way before me.'
'I the Lord do not change; so you, descendants of Jacob, are not destroyed.'
God accuses the people of robbing Him in tithes and offerings.
'Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse... see if I will not throw open the floodgates of heaven.'
Those who feared the Lord talked together; a scroll of remembrance was written.

4.title: 'Surely the day is coming; it will burn like a furnace.'
'But for you who revere my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays.'
'I will send the prophet Elijah to you before that great and dreadful day of the Lord comes.'
'He will turn the hearts of the parents to their children, and the hearts of the children to their parents.'

1.title: Genealogy of Jesus Christ, tracing His lineage from Abraham through David to Joseph.
The birth of Jesus; Mary is found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
An angel appears to Joseph in a dream, instructing him to take Mary as his wife.
Prophecy fulfilled: 'The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel.'

2.title: Wise men from the East visit Jerusalem seeking the newborn King of the Jews.
Herod secretly meets the wise men, asking them to report back.
The Magi find Jesus, worship Him, and present gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Joseph is warned in a dream to flee to Egypt to escape Herod's plot.
Herod orders the massacre of all boys two years old and under in Bethlehem.
After Herod's death, Joseph is told to return to Israel; they settle in Nazareth.

3.title: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness of Judea, calling for repentance.
John fulfills Isaiah's prophecy: 'A voice of one calling in the wilderness.'
Jesus deliberately seeks out John at the river, beginning his earthly ministry.
After Jesus is baptized, heaven opens, and the Spirit of God descends like a dove.

4.title: Jesus is taken into solitude to face Satan's first assault on his earthly mission.
Satan tempts Jesus to turn stones into bread; Jesus responds with Scripture.
Jesus begins His ministry in Galilee after John is imprisoned.
Jesus calls His first disciples: Peter, Andrew, James, and John.
Jesus teaches in synagogues, proclaims the good news, and heals the sick.

5.title: Jesus teaches the Beatitudes, blessing the poor in spirit, the meek, the merciful, etc.
Believers are called the salt of the earth and the light of the world.
Jesus affirms the Law and the Prophets; He has come to fulfill them.
Teachings on anger, adultery, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and love for enemies.

6.title: Instruction on giving to the needy without seeking attention.
Teaching on prayer; introduction of the Lord's Prayer.
Guidance on fasting in humility.
Teaching on storing up treasures in heaven rather than on earth.
Exhortation not to worry about life, food, or clothing; trust in God's provision.

7.title: Warning against judging others hypocritically.
Encouragement to ask, seek, and knock; God's readiness to give good gifts.
The Golden Rule: 'Do to others what you would have them do to you.'
Teaching about the narrow and wide gates; the true and false prophets.
Parable of the wise and foolish builders; importance of practicing Jesus' words.

8.title: Jesus heals a man with leprosy.
Healing of the centurion's servant; commendation of the centurion's faith.
Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law.
Jesus calms a storm on the Sea of Galilee.
Healing of two demon-possessed men in the region of the Gadarenes.

9.title: Jesus heals a paralyzed man and forgives his sins.
Jesus calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow Him.
Jesus raises a synagogue leader's daughter from the dead.
Healing of a woman who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years.
Jesus restores sight to two blind men.
Summary of Jesus' ministry of teaching, preaching, and healing.

10.title: Jesus calls His twelve disciples and gives them authority over unclean spirits and diseases.
Instructions for the mission of the twelve: preach the kingdom, heal the sick.
Warning of persecution; be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
The importance of acknowledging Jesus before others.
Teaching on the cost of discipleship and taking up one's cross.

11.title: John the Baptist sends disciples to ask if Jesus is the expected Messiah.
Jesus affirms John's role as the messenger prophesied in Scripture.
Jesus denounces cities that did not repent despite witnessing miracles.
Invitation to find rest in Jesus: 'Come to me, all who are weary and burdened.'

12.title: Jesus' disciples pick grain on the Sabbath; Pharisees accuse them of breaking the law.
Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath.
Jesus heals a demon-possessed man; Pharisees accuse Him of working by Satan's power.
Warning about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
Jesus defines His true family as those who do the will of His Father.

13.title: Jesus teaches the Parable of the Sower to the crowds.
Parable of the Weeds among the Wheat.
Parables of the Mustard Seed and the Yeast, illustrating the kingdom's growth.
Parables of the Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Value.
Jesus is rejected in His hometown of Nazareth.

14.title: Herod hears reports about Jesus; recalls how he had John the Baptist executed.
Jesus feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.
Jesus walks on water; Peter briefly walks on water but begins to sink.
Many are healed when Jesus reaches Gennesaret.

15.title: Pharisees question Jesus about His disciples not washing hands before eating.
Jesus rebukes them for honoring God with lips but hearts far away.
Jesus heals the daughter of a Canaanite woman who demonstrates great faith.
Jesus feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few small fish.

16.title: Jesus asks His disciples who people say He is; Peter confesses Him as the Christ.
Jesus blesses Peter and speaks of building His church.
Jesus predicts His suffering, death, and resurrection.
Teaching on discipleship: denying oneself and taking up the cross.

17.title: Jesus is transfigured on a mountain before Peter, James, and John.
Moses and Elijah appear, talking with Jesus.
Jesus heals a demon-possessed boy whom the disciples could not heal.
Second prediction of Jesus' death and resurrection.
Jesus teaches Peter about paying the temple tax.

18.title: Disciples ask who is the greatest in the kingdom; Jesus emphasizes humility.
Warning against causing little ones who believe in Him to stumble.
Parable of the Lost Sheep; God's concern for the stray.
Instructions on dealing with sin in the church community.
Parable of the Unforgiving Servant; teaching on limitless forgiveness.

19.title: Pharisees question Jesus about divorce; He emphasizes the sanctity of marriage.
Jesus welcomes little children and blesses them.
Encounter with the rich young man; challenge to give up wealth and follow Jesus.
Jesus teaches about the difficulty for the rich to enter the kingdom of heaven.

20.title: Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard; teaching on God's grace.
Third prediction of Jesus' death and resurrection.
Request of James and John's mother for her sons to sit at Jesus' right and left.
Teaching on servant leadership: 'Whoever wants to become great must be a servant.'
Jesus heals two blind men near Jericho.

21.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a donkey; fulfillment of prophecy.
Jesus cleanses the temple, driving out money changers.
Jesus curses a fig tree; it withers, symbolizing unfruitfulness.
Religious leaders question Jesus' authority.
Parable of the Two Sons; obedience to the Father's will.
Parable of the Tenants; rejection of the Son.

22.title: Parable of the Wedding Banquet; invitation to the kingdom.
Pharisees try to trap Jesus with a question about paying taxes to Caesar.
Sadducees question Jesus about the resurrection.
An expert in the law asks about the greatest commandment; Jesus emphasizes love for God and neighbor.
Jesus questions the Pharisees about the Messiah being David's son.

23.title: Jesus warns the crowds about the hypocrisy of the teachers of the law and Pharisees.
Seven woes pronounced against the hypocritical religious leaders.
Jesus laments over Jerusalem's rejection of God's messengers.

24.title: Jesus predicts the destruction of the temple.
Disciples ask about the signs of His coming and the end of the age.
Jesus describes wars, famines, earthquakes, and persecution.
Mention of the 'abomination of desolation' spoken of by Daniel.
The coming of the Son of Man will be visible like lightning.
No one knows the day or hour; be watchful and ready.

25.title: Parable of the Ten Virgins; importance of being prepared.
Parable of the Talents; stewardship and accountability.
The Son of Man will judge the nations; separation of sheep and goats.
Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for Me.

26.title: Religious leaders plot to arrest and kill Jesus.
A woman anoints Jesus with expensive perfume at Bethany.
Judas agrees to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
The Last Supper; Jesus shares Passover with His disciples.
Institution of the Lord's Supper; Jesus speaks of His body and blood.
Jesus prays in Gethsemane; His anguish and submission to the Father's will.
Jesus is arrested; Judas betrays Him with a kiss.
Jesus faces the Sanhedrin; Peter denies knowing Him three times.

27.title: Jesus is handed over to Pilate, the Roman governor.
Judas regrets his betrayal and hangs himself.
Jesus before Pilate; He remains mostly silent.
Crowd chooses Barabbas to be released instead of Jesus.
Jesus is flogged and handed over to be crucified.
Soldiers mock Jesus, placing a crown of thorns on His head.
Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; soldiers cast lots for His garments.
Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries out and yields His spirit.
The temple curtain is torn; the earth shakes; tombs break open.
The centurion declares, 'Surely He was the Son of God.'
Jesus is buried in a tomb by Joseph of Arimathea.

28.title: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary visit the tomb; an angel announces Jesus' resurrection.
Jesus appears to the women; they worship Him.
Guards report the empty tomb; chief priests bribe them to spread a false story.
Jesus meets His disciples on a mountain in Galilee.
Jesus gives the Great Commission: 'Go and make disciples of all nations.'
'And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.'

1.title: Introduction to the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
John the Baptist prepares the way, preaching a baptism of repentance.
Mark's brief note of Jesus' baptism, marking the start of his public ministry.
Jesus is tempted in the wilderness for forty days.
Jesus begins His ministry in Galilee, proclaiming the good news.
Jesus calls His first disciples: Simon (Peter) and Andrew, then James and John.
Jesus teaches in the synagogue at Capernaum and casts out an unclean spirit.
Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others.
Jesus prays in a solitary place; continues preaching and healing throughout Galilee.
Jesus heals a man with leprosy, instructing him to tell no one.

2.title: Jesus heals a paralyzed man lowered through the roof; forgives his sins.
Jesus calls Levi (Matthew), a tax collector, to follow Him.
Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners; criticized by the Pharisees.
Questioned about fasting; Jesus speaks about new wine in new wineskins.
Disciples pick grain on the Sabbath; Jesus declares, 'The Sabbath was made for man.'

3.title: Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath; Pharisees plot against Him.
Jesus appoints twelve apostles to preach and have authority over demons.
Jesus' family thinks He is out of His mind; teachers of the law accuse Him of being possessed.
Warning about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
Jesus redefines His family as those who do God's will.

4.title: Jesus teaches the Parable of the Sower to the crowds.
Explanation of why He speaks in parables.
Jesus explains the Parable of the Sower to His disciples.
Parable of the Lamp on a Stand; teachings on hearing and understanding.
Parable of the Growing Seed; the kingdom of God grows mysteriously.
Parable of the Mustard Seed; the kingdom starts small but grows large.
Jesus calms a storm on the Sea of Galilee.

5.title: Jesus heals a man possessed by a legion of demons in the region of the Gerasenes.
Jairus, a synagogue leader, pleads for his dying daughter.
A woman with a bleeding condition is healed by touching Jesus' garment.
News arrives that Jairus's daughter has died; Jesus tells him to believe.
Jesus raises Jairus's daughter from the dead.

6.title: Jesus is rejected in His hometown of Nazareth.
Jesus sends out the Twelve Apostles two by two, giving them authority over impure spirits.
Herod hears about Jesus; believes John the Baptist, whom he beheaded, has been raised.
The apostles return; Jesus invites them to rest.
Jesus feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.
Jesus walks on water; the disciples are amazed.
Many are healed when Jesus and His disciples land at Gennesaret.

7.title: Pharisees criticize Jesus' disciples for eating with unwashed hands.
Jesus rebukes them for honoring God with lips while hearts are far away.
Teaching that what comes out of a person defiles them, not what goes in.
Jesus heals the daughter of a Syrophoenician woman who demonstrates faith.
