Jesus heals a deaf and mute man in the region of Decapolis.

8.title: Jesus feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few small fish.
Pharisees demand a sign from heaven; Jesus refuses and warns about their yeast (teaching).
Jesus heals a blind man at Bethsaida in stages.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Messiah at Caesarea Philippi.
Jesus predicts His suffering, death, and resurrection.
Teaching on discipleship: denying oneself and taking up the cross.

9.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John; Moses and Elijah appear.
Jesus heals a boy possessed by an impure spirit; the disciples couldn't drive it out.
Second prediction of Jesus' death and resurrection.
Disciples argue about who is the greatest; Jesus teaches about being servant of all.
Warning against causing others to stumble; teaching on the seriousness of sin.

10.title: Jesus teaches about divorce; emphasizes the sanctity of marriage.
Jesus blesses little children, saying the kingdom belongs to such as these.
Encounter with the rich young man; challenge to give up wealth and follow Jesus.
Teaching on the difficulty for the rich to enter the kingdom of God.
Third prediction of Jesus' death and resurrection.
James and John request to sit at Jesus' right and left in glory.
Teaching on servant leadership: 'The Son of Man came to serve and give His life as a ransom.'
Jesus heals blind Bartimaeus in Jericho.

11.title: Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a colt; crowds shout 'Hosanna!'
Jesus curses a fig tree for having no fruit.
Jesus clears the temple courts of money changers and merchants.
The withered fig tree is seen; teaching on faith and prayer.
Religious leaders question Jesus' authority; He responds with a question about John's baptism.

12.title: Parable of the Tenants; rejection of the Son by the vineyard workers.
Pharisees and Herodians try to trap Jesus with a question about paying taxes to Caesar.
Sadducees question Jesus about the resurrection; He corrects their misunderstanding.
A teacher of the law asks about the greatest commandment; Jesus emphasizes love for God and neighbor.
Jesus questions how the Messiah can be David's son.
Warning against the teachers of the law who seek honor.
The widow's offering of two small coins is praised by Jesus.

13.title: Jesus predicts the destruction of the temple.
Disciples ask about the signs of the end times.
Jesus warns about false messiahs, wars, earthquakes, and persecution.
Mention of the 'abomination of desolation'; instructions to flee.
Description of cosmic disturbances and the coming of the Son of Man.
No one knows the day or hour; be watchful and alert.

14.title: Chief priests and scribes plot to arrest and kill Jesus.
A woman anoints Jesus with expensive perfume at Bethany.
Judas agrees to betray Jesus to the chief priests.
Preparation for the Passover meal; Jesus eats with His disciples.
Institution of the Lord's Supper; Jesus speaks of His body and blood.
Jesus predicts Peter's denial; they go to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus prays in Gethsemane; disciples fall asleep.
Jesus is betrayed by Judas and arrested.
Jesus faces the Sanhedrin; false witnesses testify against Him.
Peter denies Jesus three times; remembers Jesus' prediction.

15.title: Jesus is brought before Pilate; accused by chief priests.
Pilate offers to release Jesus or Barabbas; crowd chooses Barabbas.
Pilate has Jesus flogged and hands Him over to be crucified.
Soldiers mock Jesus, dressing Him in purple and placing a crown of thorns on His head.
Simon of Cyrene carries Jesus' cross.
Jesus is crucified at Golgotha; crucified between two rebels.
Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries out and dies.
The temple curtain is torn; the centurion acknowledges Jesus as the Son of God.
Joseph of Arimathea asks for Jesus' body and lays it in a tomb.

16.title: Women visit the tomb after the Sabbath and find the stone rolled away.
An angel tells them Jesus has risen and instructs them to tell the disciples.
Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene; she tells the others, but they do not believe.
Jesus appears to two disciples walking in the country.
Jesus appears to the Eleven; rebukes them for unbelief.
Jesus gives the Great Commission: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel.'
Jesus ascends into heaven and sits at the right hand of God.
The disciples preach everywhere; the Lord works with them, confirming the word with signs.

1.title: Introduction to the orderly account of events fulfilled among us.
Angel Gabriel announces to Zechariah that his wife Elizabeth will bear a son, John.
Gabriel visits Mary, announcing she will conceive Jesus, the Son of the Most High.
Mary visits Elizabeth; John leaps in her womb; Mary praises God (Magnificat).
Birth of John the Baptist; Zechariah's speech is restored; he prophesies (Benedictus).

2.title: Jesus is born in Bethlehem during the census decreed by Caesar Augustus.
Shepherds receive angelic announcement of Jesus' birth; they visit Him.
Jesus is circumcised and presented at the temple; Simeon and Anna prophesy.
At age twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple, astounding teachers with His understanding.

3.title: John the Baptist preaches a baptism of repentance; quotes Isaiah about the voice in the wilderness.
John speaks of one more powerful coming after him; he baptizes Jesus.
Heaven opens at Jesus' baptism; the Holy Spirit descends like a dove.
Genealogy of Jesus traced back to Adam, emphasizing His connection to all humanity.

4.title: Luke's account of the wilderness temptation, lasting forty days under the Spirit's leading.
Jesus begins teaching in Galilee; gains praise from all.
In Nazareth, Jesus reads Isaiah's prophecy and declares its fulfillment.
He is rejected in Nazareth; moves on to Capernaum.
Jesus drives out an impure spirit; heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others.

5.title: Jesus calls Peter, James, and John after a miraculous catch of fish.
He heals a man with leprosy; news about Him spreads.
Jesus heals a paralyzed man lowered through the roof; forgives his sins.
Jesus calls Levi (Matthew) the tax collector; eats with sinners; criticized by Pharisees.

6.title: Disciples pick grain on the Sabbath; Jesus declares Himself Lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus heals a man with a shriveled hand on the Sabbath.
Jesus prays all night; chooses twelve apostles.
Sermon on the Plain: Beatitudes, love for enemies, judging others.
Parable of the Wise and Foolish Builders; importance of practicing Jesus' words.

7.title: Jesus heals the centurion's servant; commends the centurion's faith.
Jesus raises the widow's son in Nain; crowd is filled with awe.
John the Baptist sends disciples to ask if Jesus is the Messiah.
Jesus speaks highly of John; declares him greatest among those born of women.
A sinful woman anoints Jesus' feet; He teaches about forgiveness and love.

8.title: Jesus travels from town to town proclaiming the good news; accompanied by the Twelve and women supporters.
Parable of the Sower; explanation to His disciples.
Jesus calms a storm on the lake; disciples marvel at His authority.
He heals a demon-possessed man in the region of the Gerasenes.
Jesus heals a woman with bleeding and raises Jairus's daughter from the dead.

9.title: Jesus sends out the Twelve with power and authority over demons and diseases.
Feeding of the five thousand with five loaves and two fish.
Peter confesses Jesus as God's Messiah.
Jesus predicts His suffering, death, and resurrection.
Transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain with Moses and Elijah appearing.
Disciples argue about who is the greatest; Jesus teaches about humility.

10.title: Jesus appoints seventy-two others to go ahead of Him two by two.
They return with joy; Jesus rejoices in the Spirit.
Expert in the law asks about eternal life; Jesus tells the Parable of the Good Samaritan.
Jesus visits Mary and Martha; teaches about priorities and listening to His word.

11.title: Disciples ask Jesus to teach them to pray; He gives the Lord's Prayer.
Parable of the Friend at Midnight; encouragement to persistent prayer.
Jesus drives out a mute demon; accused of working by Beelzebul.
Jesus speaks about the sign of Jonah and the need for repentance.
Woes pronounced against Pharisees and experts in the law for hypocrisy.

12.title: Jesus warns about the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Exhortation not to fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.
Parable of the Rich Fool; warning against greed.
Teaching not to worry about life's needs; seek God's kingdom.
Parable of the Faithful Servant; be ready for the Master's return.

13.title: Call to repentance; Parable of the Barren Fig Tree.
Jesus heals a crippled woman on the Sabbath; criticized by the synagogue leader.
Parables of the Mustard Seed and Yeast; illustrating the kingdom's growth.
Teaching about the narrow door; urgency to enter the kingdom.
Pharisees warn Jesus about Herod; Jesus laments over Jerusalem.

14.title: Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath at a Pharisee's house.
Parable of the Wedding Feast; teaching on humility.
Parable of the Great Banquet; many invited, few accept.
Cost of discipleship; carrying one's cross; counting the cost.
Teaching about salt losing its saltiness; importance of being effective disciples.

15.title: Tax collectors and sinners gather around Jesus; Pharisees criticize Him.
Parable of the Lost Sheep; rejoicing over one sinner who repents.
Parable of the Lost Coin; the value of each person to God.
Parable of the Prodigal Son; themes of repentance and forgiveness.

16.title: Parable of the Shrewd Manager; teaching on wise use of resources.
'No servant can serve two masters'; God versus money.
Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus; consequences of neglecting the needy.

17.title: Warnings about causing others to stumble; teaching on forgiveness.
Jesus heals ten men with leprosy; only one returns to give thanks.
Teaching about the coming of the kingdom of God; suddenness of the Son of Man's day.

18.title: Parable of the Persistent Widow; encouragement to pray persistently.
Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector; humility in prayer.
Jesus welcomes little children; kingdom belongs to such as these.
Rich ruler asks about eternal life; challenged to sell everything and follow Jesus.
Jesus predicts His death and resurrection a third time.
Jesus heals a blind beggar near Jericho.

19.title: Jesus meets Zacchaeus, a tax collector; salvation comes to his house.
Parable of the Ten Minas; responsibility and accountability.
Triumphal entry into Jerusalem; crowds praise God.
Jesus weeps over Jerusalem, predicting its destruction.
Jesus cleanses the temple, driving out merchants.

20.title: Religious leaders question Jesus' authority; He counters with a question about John's baptism.
Parable of the Tenants; rejection of the Son by vineyard workers.
Question about paying taxes to Caesar; 'Give to Caesar what is Caesar's.'
Sadducees question Jesus about the resurrection; He teaches about life after death.
Jesus poses a question on Messiahship, challenging the assumption that the Christ is merely David's heir.
Warning against the teachers of the law who seek honor and exploit others.

21.title: Jesus observes a widow giving two small coins; praises her offering.
Jesus predicts the destruction of the temple.
Disciples ask about signs of the end; Jesus speaks of wars, disasters, persecution.
Warning about Jerusalem's impending siege and destruction.
Signs in the heavens; the coming of the Son of Man.
Exhortation to watchfulness and prayer.

22.title: Plot to kill Jesus; Judas agrees to betray Him.
Preparation for the Passover meal; the Last Supper.
Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper; speaks of the new covenant.
Disciples argue about greatness; Jesus teaches about servanthood.
Jesus predicts Peter's denial; encourages him to strengthen others.
Jesus prays on the Mount of Olives; disciples fall asleep.
Jesus is arrested; Peter denies knowing Him three times.
Jesus is brought before the Sanhedrin; they question His identity.

23.title: Jesus is brought before Pilate; accused of subverting the nation.
Pilate sends Jesus to Herod; Herod mocks Him and sends Him back.
Pilate seeks to release Jesus; crowd demands crucifixion.
Simon of Cyrene carries Jesus' cross.
Jesus is crucified between two criminals.
Jesus prays, 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.'
One criminal mocks Jesus; the other asks to be remembered in His kingdom.
Darkness covers the land; Jesus dies; the centurion praises God.
Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus in a tomb.

24.title: Women visit the tomb on the first day of the week; find it empty.
Angels announce that Jesus has risen.
Jesus appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus; they recognize Him in the breaking of bread.
Jesus appears to His disciples; shows them His hands and feet.
Jesus explains how Scripture is fulfilled in Him.
Jesus ascends into heaven; disciples return to Jerusalem with joy.

1.title: John's gospel opens by naming Christ as the eternal Logos sharing the very nature of God.
The Word identified as the source of both biological life and spiritual illumination.
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us; we have seen His glory.
John the Baptist testifies about himself and denies being the Messiah.
John declares Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
First disciples follow Jesus: Andrew and another disciple.
Andrew brings his brother Simon (Peter) to Jesus.
Jesus calls Philip and Nathanael to follow Him.

2.title: Jesus attends a wedding in Cana; performs His first miracle by turning water into wine.
Jesus goes to Jerusalem for Passover; cleanses the temple by driving out merchants.
Religious leaders ask for a sign; Jesus speaks of destroying the temple and raising it in three days.

3.title: Nicodemus, a Pharisee, comes to Jesus at night to discuss His teachings.
Jesus tells Nicodemus that no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.
'For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son.'
John the Baptist testifies about Jesus, stating 'He must become greater; I must become less.'

4.title: Jesus travels through Samaria; meets a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well.
Jesus offers her 'living water' leading to eternal life.
Jesus redefines true worship as inward and Spirit-led rather than tied to a place.
Many Samaritans believe in Jesus because of the woman's testimony.
Jesus heals the royal official's son in Cana from a distance.

5.title: Jesus heals a man who had been invalid for 38 years at the Pool of Bethesda.
The healing occurs on the Sabbath; Jewish leaders question the man and Jesus.
Jesus explains His relationship with the Father; the Son can do nothing by Himself.
Those who hear His word and believe have eternal life and will not be judged.

6.title: Jesus feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish.
Jesus walks on water; calms the fears of His disciples.
Crowds seek Jesus; He teaches about the bread of life.
'I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never go hungry.'
Many disciples turn away; Peter confesses, 'You have the words of eternal life.'

7.title: Jesus goes to the Festival of Tabernacles in secret.
He teaches in the temple courts; people marvel at His wisdom.
'Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.'
Division among the people about who Jesus is.

8.title: Jesus forgives a woman caught in adultery; challenges those without sin to cast the first stone.
'I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will never walk in darkness.'
Teaching about the truth setting believers free.
'Before Abraham was born, I am!'

9.title: Jesus heals a man born blind; disciples question whose sin caused his blindness.
Jesus makes mud with saliva, puts it on the man's eyes, and tells him to wash.
Pharisees investigate the healing; the man testifies about Jesus.
Jesus reveals Himself to the healed man; he believes and worships Jesus.

10.title: Jesus describes Himself as the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep.
'I am the gate; whoever enters through me will be saved.'
Jesus claims the shepherd image and stakes it on his coming self-sacrifice.
The mark of belonging to Christ: recognition, intimacy, and obedience.
Jesus' bluntest claim to oneness with the Father.

11.title: Lazarus, brother of Mary and Martha, is sick; Jesus delays visiting.
'I am the resurrection and the life; whoever believes in me will live.'
Jesus weeps at Lazarus's tomb.
Jesus calls Lazarus out of the tomb; Lazarus is raised from the dead.
Jewish leaders plot to kill Jesus after this miracle.

12.title: Mary anoints Jesus' feet with expensive perfume; Judas objects.
Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a donkey; crowds shout 'Hosanna!'
Jesus speaks about His impending death and glorification.
'And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.'

13.title: Jesus washes His disciples' feet, demonstrating servanthood.
Jesus predicts His betrayal; Judas leaves to betray Him.
Christ's defining commandment: love modeled on his own sacrificial love.
Jesus predicts Peter's denial before the rooster crows.

14.title: On the eve of his arrest, Jesus calms the disciples and invites their trust.
'I am the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me.'
Promise of the Holy Spirit as the Advocate.
'Peace I leave with you; my peace I give you.'

15.title: The vine metaphor introduced — Christ as source, the Father as caretaker.
'I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit.'
'My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you.'
Jesus prepares the disciples for hostility, framing it as continuity with his own rejection.

16.title: Jesus explains that it is for their good that He is going away; the Advocate will come.
The Spirit of truth will guide them into all truth.
Their grief will turn to joy; analogy of a woman in labor.
'In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.'

17.title: Jesus prays for Himself, asking to be glorified so He may glorify the Father.
He prays for His disciples, for their protection and unity.
Jesus prays for all believers, that they may be one as He and the Father are one.
Desire for believers to be with Him and see His glory.

18.title: Jesus is betrayed by Judas and arrested in the Garden of Gethsemane.
Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant; Jesus is taken to Annas.
Peter denies knowing Jesus three times.
Jesus is brought before Pilate; He declares His kingdom is not of this world.

19.title: Jesus is flogged; soldiers mock Him with a crown of thorns.
Pilate finds no basis for a charge but the crowd demands crucifixion.
Jesus is led to Golgotha; crucified between two others.
Jesus entrusts His mother to the beloved disciple.
Jesus says, 'It is finished,' and gives up His spirit.
Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bury Jesus' body in a new tomb.

20.title: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty; tells Peter and John.
Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene; she recognizes Him when He says her name.
Jesus appears to His disciples, shows them His wounds, and gives them peace.
Thomas doubts until he sees Jesus; exclaims, 'My Lord and my God!'
Purpose of the Gospel: that readers may believe Jesus is the Messiah and have life in His name.

21.title: Jesus appears to disciples by the Sea of Galilee; miracle of the large catch of fish.
Jesus reinstates Peter by asking three times if he loves Him; commands him to feed His sheep.
Jesus predicts Peter's martyrdom.
Closing acknowledgment that the gospel can only sample what Jesus did.

1.title: Introduction by Luke, summarizing Jesus' teachings after His resurrection.
Jesus instructs the disciples to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit.
Promise of power through the Holy Spirit to be witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
Peter addresses the disciples regarding the need to replace Judas Iscariot.
The disciples pray and cast lots to choose Matthias as the replacement apostle.

2.title: The Holy Spirit descends on the disciples during Pentecost.
Disciples begin to speak in different tongues as the Spirit enables them.
Peter stands up and addresses the crowd, explaining the fulfillment of prophecy.
Peter calls for repentance and baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
About three thousand people are added to the church.

3.title: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful.
Peter declares that the healing is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
The healed man enters the temple walking, leaping, and praising God.
Peter urges the crowd to repent and turn to God for their sins.

4.title: Peter and John are confronted by the Sanhedrin after the healing.
Peter declares that salvation is found in no one else except Jesus Christ.
The believers are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak God's word boldly.

5.title: Ananias and Sapphira lie about the proceeds of their land sale and die.
Peter and the apostles continue to preach despite persecution.
The apostles are flogged and ordered not to speak in the name of Jesus.

6.title: The early church faces complaints about the distribution to widows.
The apostles appoint seven deacons to handle daily distributions.

7.title: Stephen recounts the history of Israel and accuses the Jewish leaders of resisting the Holy Spirit.
Stephen is stoned to death, becoming the first Christian martyr.

8.title: Persecution scatters the believers throughout Judea and Samaria.
Philip is guided by an angel to evangelize in Samaria and to the Ethiopian eunuch.

9.title: Saul encounters a bright light on the road to Damascus and is blinded.
Ananias is instructed by the Lord to restore Saul's sight.
Saul begins to preach in Damascus about Jesus.

10.title: Peter has a vision of a sheet with unclean animals, symbolizing the acceptance of Gentiles.
Peter declares that God shows no partiality, accepting people from every nation.
The Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile believers at Cornelius' house, confirming their salvation.

11.title: Believers from scattered regions begin preaching in Antioch, leading to significant growth.
Barnabas brings Saul to Antioch, where they teach and a large number believe.
The church in Antioch sends aid to the brethren in Judea during a famine.

12.title: An angel frees Peter from prison during Herod's persecution of the church.
The church prays fervently for Peter's safety and he is miraculously released.

13.title: The Holy Spirit calls Barnabas and Saul for missionary work during worship in Antioch.
Barnabas and Saul are sent out with John Mark to preach the Gospel in Cyprus and Asia Minor.

14.title: Paul and Barnabas preach in Iconium, facing both acceptance and opposition.
Paul heals a crippled man in Lystra, leading the crowd to believe they are gods.
Paul and Barnabas return to Antioch, reporting many conversions and the growth of the church.

15.title: Peter argues that Gentile believers should not be burdened with the law of Moses.
James concludes that Gentiles need not follow the entire Law of Moses, but should abstain from certain practices.
The council issues a letter with guidelines for Gentile believers, promoting unity in the church.

16.title: Paul receives a vision of a man from Macedonia calling for help, prompting their journey west.
Paul and Silas invite the Philippian jailer to believe in Jesus after an earthquake frees them from prison.
The Philippian jailer and his household are baptized following their conversion.

17.title: Paul preaches in the synagogue in Thessalonica, leading to both conversions and opposition.
The Bereans are commended for examining the Scriptures daily to verify Paul's teachings.
In Athens, Paul addresses the Areopagus, speaking about the unknown God and the resurrection.

18.title: Paul meets Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth and partners with them in ministry.
Paul receives a vision encouraging him to continue preaching despite opposition.
The Lord persuades a great number to believe, leading to the growth of the church in Corinth.

19.title: God performs extraordinary miracles through Paul in Ephesus, demonstrating His power.
A riot breaks out in Ephesus led by silversmiths opposing Paul's teachings against idol worship.
Paul leaves Ephesus after three years, having significantly impacted the city's spiritual landscape.

20.title: Paul celebrates the first Eucharist with the Ephesian elders on the first day of the week.
Paul speaks plainly about his upcoming journey to Jerusalem, knowing of the dangers ahead.
Paul emphasizes that his goal is to finish the race and complete the task of ministry for the Lord Jesus.

21.title: Paul meets prophets who predict his imprisonment in Jerusalem.
Paul arrives at the temple and declares his innocence, causing a stir among the crowd.
Paul is seized by a mob and arrested after his preaching incites opposition.

22.title: Paul recounts his conversion experience to the crowd, emphasizing his transformation.
Paul explains that he was sent to the Gentiles as per God's revelation.

23.title: Jesus appears to Paul in a vision, encouraging him to testify about the Gospel.
A plot to kill Paul within the Sanhedrin is uncovered, leading to his transfer to Caesarea.

24.title: Paul testifies about his faith in Jesus Christ before Governor Felix.
Felix adjourns the proceedings, promising to send for Paul when convenient.

25.title: Paul invokes his right as a Roman citizen to appeal to Caesar, ensuring a fair trial.
King Agrippa expresses interest in Paul's case and questions his beliefs.

26.title: Jesus commissions Paul to be a witness to the Gentiles during his defense.
Agrippa concludes that Paul could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.

27.title: An angel assures Paul that he will stand before Caesar despite the impending shipwreck.
After a shipwreck, all aboard survive and reach safety on the island of Malta.

28.title: Paul is bitten by a viper but suffers no harm, leading the crowd to regard him as a murderer but seeing his miraculous survival.
Paul stays in Rome for two years, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ.

1.title: Paul introduces himself as a servant of Christ, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God.
Paul addresses the letter to all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints.
Paul expresses that he is not ashamed of the gospel, as it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes.
Introduces the theme of righteousness by faith, which is revealed in the gospel.
Explains that God's invisible qualities are evident in creation, leaving people without excuse for their unbelief.

2.title: Warns against taking God's kindness for granted, emphasizing that His kindness is meant to lead to repentance.
States that God shows no favoritism and judges everyone impartially based on their actions.
Describes how God's judgment will be according to the truth of the gospel, regardless of one's knowledge of the law.

3.title: Highlights that no one is righteous on their own, emphasizing the universal nature of sin.
Affirms that all have sinned and fall short of God's glory, establishing the need for salvation.
Explains that all are justified freely by God's grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus.
Emphasizes that a person is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.
Affirms that both Jews and Gentiles are justified by the same faith in Christ.

4.title: Uses Abraham's belief in God as an example of being credited as righteous through faith.
Clarifies that a person is not justified by works but by faith, referencing Abraham's experience.
Argues that the promise to Abraham extends to all who believe, not just those under the law.

5.title: Explains that believers have peace with God through their justification by faith.
Highlights God's love demonstrated through Christ's sacrificial death while humanity was still sinful.
Describes how sin entered the world through one man, Adam, and brought death to all.
Contrasts the reign of sin through one man with the gift of grace that leads to righteousness and life through many.

6.title: Addresses the misconception that believers should continue sinning to experience God's grace.
Describes baptism as a symbol of being buried with Christ into death and raised to new life.
Affirms that believers are not under the law but under grace, freeing them from sin's dominance.

7.title: Explains that believers have died to the law through the body of Christ and are now bound to serve Him.
Expresses the inner conflict with sin, highlighting the struggle even after understanding the law.

8.title: Assures that there is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
Paul's confidence that providence orchestrates every circumstance toward the believer's ultimate good.
Encourages believers by stating that if God is for them, no one can stand against them.

9.title: Highlights God's authority to show mercy and compassion as He chooses.
Contrasts those who seek righteousness through the law with those who attain it through faith.
References the chosen people as a royal priesthood, emphasizing God's selection.

10.title: Explains that confessing Jesus as Lord and believing in His resurrection leads to salvation.
Affirms that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, extending salvation to all.
States that faith comes from hearing the message about Christ.

11.title: Emphasizes that salvation cannot be based on works but is a result of God's grace.
Affirms that all things are from God, through Him, and for Him, highlighting His sovereignty.

12.title: Encourages believers to offer their bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God.
Advises not to conform to worldly patterns but to be transformed by renewing the mind.
Calls for sincere love, hatred of evil, and clinging to what is good.
Paul's paradoxical strategy: defeat malice not by retaliation but by deliberate kindness.

13.title: Urges believers not to grumble against one another, warning of judgment for such behavior.
Explains that the Spirit of life has set believers free from the law of sin and death.

14.title: Encourages living for the Lord in all circumstances, whether in life or death.
Advises keeping personal beliefs private to maintain harmony within the community.

15.title: Calls for strong believers to bear with the failings of the weak and not seek personal pleasure.
Encourages acceptance among believers, just as Christ accepted them, to glorify God.
Describes Paul's mission to preach the gospel to the Gentiles.
Details plans to send Barnabas and Saul to Antioch to deliver a financial contribution.

16.title: Paul appoints Timothy as his companion for ministry.
Describes Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns to God while imprisoned, leading to miraculous events.
Highlights the invitation to believe in the Lord Jesus for salvation extended to the Philippian jailer.
Mentions the baptism of the Philippian jailer and his household following their conversion.

17.title: Details Paul's reasoning with Jews and God-fearing Greeks in Thessalonica's synagogue.
Commends the Bereans for eagerly receiving the message and examining the Scriptures daily.
Describes Paul's speech at the Areopagus in Athens, addressing their altar to an unknown god.
Affirms that in Christ, all find their purpose, highlighting the universality of His mission.

18.title: Narrates the Lord speaking to Paul in a vision, encouraging him not to fear.
Introduces Apollos, an eloquent speaker, who is instructed by Priscilla and Aquila to preach accurately.
Highlights the growth of the Corinthian church as the Lord adds to their number daily those who are being saved.

19.title: Describes God performing extraordinary miracles through Paul in Ephesus, demonstrating His power.
Accounts for a riot in Ephesus led by silversmiths opposing Paul's teachings against idol worship.
Mentions the shaking of the city but notes that Paul continues his ministry undeterred.

20.title: Details Paul's travels through Macedonia and Greece, strengthening the believers.
Paul emphasizes that his life is focused on finishing the ministry task given by the Lord Jesus.
Paul charges the Ephesian elders to watch over themselves and the flock entrusted to them by the Holy Spirit.

21.title: Describes Paul and his companions traveling to Jerusalem despite warnings of impending dangers.
Paul encourages the believers in Jerusalem, promising to return after fulfilling his mission.
Narrates Paul being seized by the crowd and taken into custody after his preaching incites opposition.

22.title: Paul recounts his conversion experience on the road to Damascus, emphasizing his transformation.
Explains that God sent him to preach to the Gentiles, highlighting his divine mission.

23.title: Describes Jesus appearing to Paul in a vision, encouraging him to testify about the gospel.
Details a plot to kill Paul within the Sanhedrin, leading to his transfer to Caesarea.

24.title: Paul defends himself before Governor Felix, explaining his faith in Christ.
Felix adjourns the proceedings, keeping Paul in custody while hoping for a bribe.

25.title: Paul invokes his right as a Roman citizen to appeal to Caesar, ensuring a fair trial.
Festus discusses Paul's case with King Agrippa, explaining the situation.

26.title: Paul describes his mission to open people's eyes and turn them from darkness to light.
King Agrippa remarks that Paul could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.

27.title: Paul remains confident in God's plan despite the impending shipwreck, declaring he will stand before Caesar.
After a shipwreck, all aboard survive and reach safety on the island of Malta.

28.title: Describes Paul being bitten by a viper but suffering no harm, leading the crowd to reconsider their views.
Paul stays in Rome for two years, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ.

1.title: Paul greets the church in Corinth, called to be saints together with all who call on Jesus.
Paul urges unity among the Corinthians, asking them to be of one mind and avoid divisions.
Explains that Paul did not come to Corinth with eloquent speech or human wisdom but to preach Christ crucified.
Paul frames the gospel's split reception: nonsense to the lost, divine power to the saved.
Highlights that God chose the foolish and weak to shame the wise and strong, emphasizing God's power.

2.title: Paul focused on knowing Christ and preaching not with persuasive words of human wisdom but with the power of the Spirit.
Emphasizes that Paul's preaching relied on the Spirit's power, not on eloquent speech or wisdom.
States that the natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, for they are folly to them.

3.title: Paul clarifies that he planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God gave the growth.
Describes the church as God’s field, with Paul and Apollos as workers together.
Reminds believers that they are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God dwells in them.

4.title: Paul urges believers to view him and Apollos as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
Paul explains that everything belongs to them, but they are nothing without God.
Encourages believers to perform spiritual gifts with power, not merely with human effort.

5.title: Advises the church to cleanse themselves from the immoral person among them, who is akin to a little yeast leavening the whole batch.
Affirms the right of the church to judge those inside and those outside the church.

6.title: Addresses the issue of believers taking each other to court instead of resolving disputes within the church.

7.title: Paul discusses matters related to marriage, advising that it is good for a man not to marry.
Encourages each person to remain in the situation they were in when called by God.
Advises slaves to set their minds on the master, not on the things of the master.

8.title: Acknowledges that knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
Affirms that there is only one God, the Father, from whom all things came, and one Lord, Jesus Christ.
Warns that exercising knowledge might lead to the weaker brother being tempted and fall into sin.

9.title: Describes Paul's approach of becoming all things to all people to save some.
Explains that Paul becomes weak to win the weak, becoming a servant to all to gain more.
Encourages believers to run the race with discipline, aiming to receive an imperishable crown.

10.title: Warns believers not to become proud when they succeed, reminding them that God is testing them.
Assures that God does not allow believers to be tempted beyond what they can bear and provides a way out.
Encourages doing everything for the glory of God, whether eating, drinking, or anything else.

11.title: Calls believers to imitate him as he imitates Christ.
Paul recounts the tradition he received regarding the Lord’s Supper.
Advises believers to examine themselves before eating to avoid judgment.

12.title: Paul opens his teaching on spiritual gifts: variety in expression, unity in source.
Describes the church as one body with many parts, each having different functions.
Encourages believers to desire the greater gifts and earnestly seek the best gifts.

13.title: Emphasizes that without love, even the most impressive spiritual gifts are meaningless.
Affirms that faith, hope, and love abide, with love being the greatest.

14.title: Encourages believers to pursue love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, especially prophecy.
States that he would rather speak five intelligible words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Calls for everything to be done decently and in order within the church gatherings.

15.title: Reiterates the gospel he preached, emphasizing its importance for salvation.
States that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures.
Affirms that Christ has been raised from the dead, becoming the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
Encourages steadfastness in the Lord’s work, knowing that labor in the Lord is not in vain.

16.title: Urges believers to be watchful, stand firm in the faith, and be courageous.
Instructs to do everything in love.
Concludes with final greetings and blessings, expressing love and grace to the believers.

1.title: Paul praises God as the source of all comfort, who comforts believers in all their troubles.
Explains that comfort allows believers to comfort others with the comfort they have received from God.
Describes the hardships Paul and his companions faced and how they were delivered by God.

2.title: Paul expresses his sorrow for causing grief and his intention to forgive the offender.
Highlights Paul's sincere motives in his ministry, contrasting with deceitful workers.
Paul rejoices that a servant of Christ is being used for the Corinthians' good, not for their harm.

3.title: Describes the believers as a letter from Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God.
The new covenant defined as a regime of liberty under the Spirit.
Encourages believers to be transformed into Christ’s image by the Spirit, with glory increasing as from one degree to another.

4.title: Uses the metaphor of treasure in jars of clay to illustrate the believers' fragile bodies housing the powerful gospel message.
Encourages believers not to lose heart, despite outward decay, because inward renewal continues day by day.
Focuses on the unseen eternal glory rather than the temporary visible hardships.

5.title: Paul's compact statement of the regenerative transformation Christ effects.
Explains that God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation, restoring the relationship between God and humanity.
Encourages believers to be ambassadors for Christ, representing Him and sharing the message of reconciliation.

6.title: Advises believers not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers, emphasizing the importance of shared values.
Affirms God's promise to dwell with believers and be their God, encouraging holiness.
Uses the metaphor of believers as a temple of the living God, urging them to cleanse themselves from impurity.

7.title: Expresses Paul's joy and comfort over the Corinthians' repentance and renewed relationship.

8.title: Encourages the Corinthians to excel in the grace of giving, inspired by the generosity of others.
Highlights that giving should be voluntary and not under compulsion, fostering grace.
Affirms that Paul's ministry is authentic and trustworthy, aiming to prove the sincerity of their love.

9.title: Teaches that whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will reap generously.
Emphasizes that each person should give what they have decided in their heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion.
Assures that God is able to bless abundantly, providing all they need to continue their generous giving.
Explains that their generosity will result in thanksgiving to God and increase their service capabilities.

10.title: Describes spiritual weapons that are powerful and able to demolish strongholds, not relying on worldly methods.
Affirms that their authority extends as far as the faith goes, aiming to reach all in Christ.
States that God is the judge of their boasting, ensuring that their claims are in line with His standards.

11.title: Paul recounts his numerous hardships and sufferings for the sake of Christ.
Describes how Paul has been made a spectacle to others, suffering for the sake of the gospel.
Explains that Paul has been frequently in danger, often on the very brink of death, to ensure the gospel is preached.

12.title: Illustrates that believers are many parts of one body, each with different functions.
Encourages embracing divine grace, which empowers believers to endure and serve.
Encourages believers to show honor to one another in love and to eagerly desire spiritual gifts.
Highlights the importance of each member's role in the body of Christ, working together in harmony.
Urges believers to carry each other's burdens, fulfilling the law of Christ.
Paul expresses his willingness to visit the Corinthians, emphasizing his desire for their well-being.
States that Paul is ready to be burdened for their progress and joy in the faith.

1.title: Paul introduces himself as an apostle not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father.
Paul expresses astonishment that the Galatians are turning to a different gospel.
'I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that the gospel I preached is not of human origin.'
Paul emphasizes that the gospel was revealed to him directly by Jesus Christ.
Paul recounts his calling by God before he was born and his separation from Judaism.

2.title: 'know that a person is not justified by the works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ.'
'I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.'
Paul asserts that pursuing righteousness through the law nullifies Christ's sacrifice.

3.title: 'Are you so foolish? After beginning by means of the Spirit, are you now trying to finish by means of the flesh?'
'There is no one righteous, not even one.'
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us.
Paul declares that in Christ every social, ethnic, and gender division is dissolved.

4.title: When the set time had fully come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.
'You are no longer a slave, but God's child; and since you are his child, God has made you also an heir.'
Paul urges the Galatians to stop being like slaves and to be children of God.

5.title: 'It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery.'
'You, my brothers and sisters, were called to be free. But do not use your freedom to indulge the flesh.'
List of the acts of the flesh contrasted with the fruit of the Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

6.title: 'Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.'
'May I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.'
Peace and mercy to all who follow this rule—to the Israel of God.

1.title: Describes Christ as the image of the invisible God and the firstborn over all creation.
Affirms that all things were created through Christ and for Him, and that He is before all things.
States that Christ is the head of the body, the church, and the firstborn from among the dead.
Highlights that through Christ, God reconciled all things to Himself, making peace through His blood shed on the cross.
Encourages holding firmly to the faith once delivered to the saints without wavering.
Explains Paul's ministry to proclaim Christ, admonish, teach everyone with all wisdom, and present everyone mature in Him.

2.title: Urges believers to continue living in Christ, being rooted and built up in Him.
Warns against being taken captive by philosophy and empty deceit, which rely on human tradition.
Affirms that in Christ, believers have been brought to fullness, having been given fullness in Him.
Advises not to let anyone judge them by what they eat or drink or with regard to religious festivals.
Warns against false humility and the worship of angels, which distracts from the head, Christ.
Explains that believers have died with Christ to the elemental spiritual forces of this world.

3.title: Encourages setting hearts on things above, where Christ is, rather than on earthly things.
Calls believers to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Advises bearing with each other and forgiving one another as the Lord has forgiven them.
Emphasizes that above all these virtues, love should bind everything together in perfect unity.
Every word and deed framed as service to Christ, marked by gratitude.
Advises doing work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men, knowing that from the Lord they will receive the inheritance.
Reminds that they serve the Lord Christ, who will reward them for their good deeds.

4.title: Encourages believers to devote themselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful.
Advises being wise in the way they act toward outsiders, making the most of every opportunity.
Calls for letting their conversation be always full of grace, seasoned with salt, so that they may know how to answer everyone.
Introduces Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, who will inform the believers about Paul’s circumstances.
Greets Epaphras, a servant of Christ Jesus who is one of the believers in Colossae.
Mentions Luke the beloved physician and Demas, who is with Paul.
Ends with final greetings and blessings, emphasizing grace to the believers.

1.title: Paul, Silas, and Timothy express gratitude to God for the Thessalonians' faith, love, and hope in Jesus Christ.
Commends their work produced by faith, labor prompted by love, and endurance inspired by hope in Christ.
Highlights that they became imitators of Paul and the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit.

2.title: Paul compares his ministry to that of a nursing mother caring for her children, demonstrating genuine love and tenderness.
Describes Paul's efforts to win the Thessalonians not by flattering words or deceit but by the Holy Spirit and sincere love.
Addresses those who persecute believers without reason, affirming that they deserve to be cursed.

3.title: Paul expresses his intense desire to see the Thessalonians again to strengthen their faith amidst opposition.
Commends Timothy for his faithful ministry and reports that the Thessalonians have turned to God from idols.
Prays for the Thessalonians to be blessed in every good work and word, and to be strengthened in their faith.

4.title: Emphasizes God's will for believers to be sanctified and avoid sexual immorality.
Affirms that God has called believers to live a holy life, rejecting impurity.
Comforts believers regarding those who have died, assuring them of the resurrection through Jesus Christ.
Describes the Lord’s return, where believers who are alive will be caught up with Him in the clouds.
Encourages rejoicing with believers who have died, comforting them by the hope of resurrection.

5.title: Assures that God did not appoint believers to suffer wrath but to receive salvation through Jesus Christ.
Encourages rejoicing always, praying continually, and giving thanks in all circumstances.
Prays for the complete sanctification of believers' spirit, soul, and body.
Paul closes the letter with his customary grace-blessing.

1.title: Paul expresses gratitude for the Thessalonians' faith, love, and endurance in affliction.
Commends their steadfastness and perseverance, highlighting their work prompted by faith.
Describes the punishment awaiting those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel.
Prays for the Thessalonians to be worthy of God's calling and to fulfill His good purpose.

2.title: Paul urges the Thessalonians not to be quickly shaken or alarmed by reports of the Lord's return.
Warns that a great rebellion must occur before the Day of the Lord and that the man of lawlessness will be revealed.
Describes the man of lawlessness as one who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship.
Affirms that the revelation of the man of lawlessness is already at work and that the Lord will destroy him with His coming.
Encourages believers to stand firm and hold their traditions unshaken, as they were taught by Paul.

3.title: Assures the Thessalonians that the Lord is faithful and will strengthen and protect them from the evil one.
Exhorts believers to work diligently and lead quiet lives, minding their own business.
Declares that those unwilling to work should not eat, emphasizing the importance of personal responsibility.
Offers final greetings, blessings of the Lord Jesus, and a benediction of peace and love.
Encourages the Thessalonians to greet all brothers and sisters with a holy kiss and to respect everyone.

1.title: Affirms the gospel as the truth and the means of salvation.
Lists those who have deviated from the faith and have been handed over to Satan.

2.title: Encourages prayers for all people, including kings and those in authority.
States that women should not teach or have authority over men in the church.

3.title: Describes the importance and responsibility of being an overseer (bishop).
Lists the qualifications for overseers, including being above reproach and self-controlled.
Outlines the qualifications for deacons, emphasizing dignity and sincerity.

4.title: Exhorts Timothy to set an example in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity.
Encourages vigilance in teaching and managing the church effectively.

5.title: Advises on respectful treatment of older men and women in the church.
Emphasizes the importance of providing for one's relatives as a sign of faith.

6.title: Warns that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
Charges Timothy to fight the good fight of faith and hold onto eternal life.
Exalts God, the King of glory, who alone is immortal and invisible.

1.title: Encourages Timothy by reminding him that God has given him a spirit of power, love, and self-discipline.
Urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony about the Lord or of Paul’s imprisonment.
Expresses Paul's confidence in the gospel despite suffering for its sake.
Admonishes Timothy to guard the good deposit entrusted to him through the Holy Spirit.

2.title: Advises Timothy to entrust what he has heard from Paul to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others.
Encourages Timothy to present himself to God as one approved, handling the word of truth accurately.
Warns against useless chatter that leads to envy and strife, urging focus on what is honorable.
Instructs Timothy to gently correct those who oppose him, showing patience and kindness.

3.title: Warns that in the last days difficult times will come, marked by selfishness and godlessness.
Describes people who have a form of godliness but deny its power, leading to hypocrisy.
Affirms that all Scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness.
States that Scripture equips believers for every good work.

4.title: Commands Timothy to preach the word, be prepared in season and out of season, and correct, rebuke, and encourage with patience and careful instruction.
Exhorts Timothy to be sober-minded, endure suffering, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill his ministry.
Declares that Paul has fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
Affirms that the Lord rescued Paul from every evil deed and will bring him safely to His heavenly kingdom.

1.title: Paul explains that he left Titus in Crete to organize what was left unfinished and appoint elders in every town.
Outlines the qualifications for an overseer, emphasizing blamelessness, self-control, and sound doctrine.
Describes the overseer's responsibility to hold firmly to the trustworthy message and to encourage others by sound doctrine.
Warns against those who are wild and crazy, full of meaningless talk and deception, rejecting authority.

2.title: Encourages Titus to teach what is appropriate to sound doctrine.
Urges older men to be temperate, worthy of respect, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and endurance.
Advises older women to be reverent in behavior, not to slander others, and to teach what is good.
Calls Titus to set an example in everything, showing integrity, dignity, and sound speech.
Urges Titus to live wisely among unbelievers, redeeming the time and being prepared to do good.
Affirms that God's grace has appeared, offering salvation to all people and training believers to renounce ungodliness.
Exhorts believers to live in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ, bearing fruit in every good work.

3.title: Reminds believers to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, and to be ready to do good.
Emphasizes that salvation comes not by righteous things we have done, but by God's mercy through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
Encourages Titus to remind the believers to be submissive, to do good works, and to avoid foolish controversies.
Warns against those who promote myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculations rather than advancing God's work.
Requests Titus to instruct certain people not to teach false doctrines or to devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies.
Expresses Paul's hope to visit Titus soon and greet him with a loving kiss.

1.title: Paul greets Philemon with grace and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Expresses Paul's reluctance to appeal personally but feels compelled by love and the gospel.
Highlights Paul's desire to take Onesimus back himself rather than compel Philemon to do so.
Acknowledges that Onesimus may have been separated from Philemon for a while but is now useful.
Requests Philemon to receive Onesimus not merely as a slave but as a beloved brother in Christ.
Assures Philemon that if he thinks differently, Paul is ready to inform him of what is to be done.
Shares Paul's personal circumstances, being in chains for the gospel of Christ.
Paul closes the brief letter with his standard grace-blessing.
Highlights that God has spoken to humanity through His Son, establishing Christ's authority.
Describes Christ as the radiance of God's glory, sustaining all things by His powerful word.
Affirms that Christ is superior to angels, having inherited a more excellent name.

2.title: Explains that Jesus shared in humanity to destroy the power of death and deliver those who were enslaved by fear.
Describes Jesus as a merciful and faithful high priest who made atonement for sins.
Affirms that Jesus is able to help those who are being tempted because He himself has been tempted.

3.title: Encourages believers to consider Jesus, worthy of glory and honor, who has been appointed by God.
States that Jesus is greater than Moses, as Moses was faithful in all God's house, but Christ is faithful over God's house.
Affirms that Christ is the apostle and high priest appointed by God, superior to Moses.

4.title: Describes the word of God as living, active, and sharper than any double-edged sword, penetrating even to dividing soul and spirit.
Encourages believers to approach God's throne of grace with confidence to receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
Highlights the great mercy and warning available to believers through Jesus Christ.

5.title: Describes how Jesus offered prayers and supplications with loud cries and tears during His earthly life.
Affirms that God designated Jesus to be a high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
Explains that mature believers have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil through practice.

6.title: Encourages believers to move beyond the elementary teachings and advance to maturity.
Warns that it is impossible to restore to repentance those who have once been enlightened and have tasted the heavenly gift.
Expresses Paul's earnest desire for the Thessalonians to excel more and more in the faith.

7.title: Introduces Melchizedek as king of Salem and priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham.
States that Jesus became a high priest not on the basis of a legal requirement concerning bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life.
Affirms that Jesus is able to save completely those who come to God through Him because He always lives to intercede for them.

9.title: Describes Christ as entering the heavenly sanctuary as our high priest, not by the blood of goats and calves but by His own blood.
Explains that Christ's blood cleanses our conscience from acts that lead to death, so that we may serve the living God.
States that Christ was sacrificed once to take away sins and will appear a second time, not to bear sin but to bring salvation.

10.title: Encourages believers to draw near to God with a sincere heart and full assurance of faith.
Exhorts believers to cleanse their hearts from wickedness and hold firmly to the hope they profess.
Urges believers to hold unswervingly to the hope they profess, for He who promised is faithful.
Encourages believers to consider how to spur one another on toward love and good deeds.

11.title: The famous biblical definition of trust as substantive certainty about unseen realities.
The author makes trust the non-negotiable condition of approach to God.
Describes the city prepared from the foundation of the world, whose architect and builder is God.
Lists examples of faith in action, such as Abraham, Moses, and others who faced trials and achieved great things.

12.title: Encourages believers to run with endurance the race set before them, fixing their eyes on Jesus.
Describes Jesus as the pioneer and perfecter of faith, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him.
Explains that God disciplines those He loves, likening it to a father disciplining his children.
Exhorts believers to pursue peace with everyone and holiness without which no one will see the Lord.

13.title: Encourages believers to continue doing what is good.
Affirms that marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept pure.
Ends with final greetings and a blessing of peace and mercy.

1.title: Encourages believers to view trials as opportunities for growth and developing perseverance.
Advises seeking wisdom from God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
Urges listeners to be doers of the word, not merely hearers, and to apply the teachings in their lives.
Warns against allowing the tongue to deceive and emphasizes controlling one's speech to prevent harm.
Defines pure and faultless religion as caring for orphans and widows in their distress and keeping oneself unstained by the world.

2.title: Warns against showing favoritism based on outward appearances, emphasizing the equality of all people.
Questions the value of faith without accompanying actions, highlighting the necessity of deeds.
States that faith by itself, if not accompanied by action, is dead.
Acknowledges belief in God but emphasizes that mere belief without deeds is insufficient.

3.title: Compares the tongue to a small fire that can set a great forest ablaze, illustrating its potential for destruction.
Highlights the inconsistency of using the same tongue to bless God and curse people made in His likeness.
Describes the characteristics of wisdom from above, which is pure, peace-loving, considerate, and full of mercy.

4.title: Addresses the root causes of conflicts and quarrels as desires that battle within individuals.
Reminds that God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Encourages submission to God, resisting the devil, and standing firm in faith.
Calls for humility before the Lord, promising that God will lift up the humble.

5.title: Warns the rich about the miseries that are coming due to their unjust accumulation of wealth.
Advises patience and steadfastness, using the farmer's wait for the valuable crop as an example.
Encourages prayer in all circumstances, whether in suffering or happiness.
Emphasizes the power of confessing sins to one another and praying for each other for healing.
Highlights the value of turning a sinner from the error of their way, saving them from death and covering a multitude of sins.

1.title: Praises God for the living hope through Jesus' resurrection, leading to an eternal inheritance.
Acknowledges trials that test faith, which is more valuable than gold and results in praise and glory.
Encourages believers to prepare their minds for action, be self-controlled, and set hope fully on grace.
Reminds believers to live in reverent fear as children of God, abstaining from sinful desires.

2.title: Declares believers as a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and God's special possession.
Urges believers to conduct themselves honorably among non-believers to glorify God.
Advises slaves to submit to their masters with respect, even those who are harsh.

3.title: Encourages wives to submit to their husbands to win them over through behavior.
Urges all to be like-minded, sympathetic, loving, compassionate, and humble.
Instructs believers to always be ready to explain their hope with gentleness and respect.

4.title: Calls for self-control and alertness because the end times are near.
Encourages believers not to be surprised by suffering but to rejoice as participants in Christ's sufferings.
Advises believers to be ashamed of sinful behavior and to glorify God through good deeds.

5.title: Advises younger people to submit to elders and everyone to clothe themselves with humility.
Encourages humility under God's mighty hand, promising that He will exalt the humble.
Urges believers to cast all anxieties on God because He cares for them.
Assures that after suffering a little, God will restore, confirm, strengthen, and establish them.
Closes with greetings to the elders and faithful believers in the church, offering peace and love.

1.title: Introduces the letter, affirming the authority of the prophets and apostles concerning Jesus Christ.
Describes the divine power that has granted believers everything necessary for life and godliness.
Encourages adding virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, mutual affection, and love to one's faith.
Emphasizes the importance of confirming the truth of the prophets through personal experience.
States that prophecy was never produced by human will but by men moved by the Holy Spirit.

2.title: Warns of false prophets and teachers who will secretly introduce destructive heresies.
Describes how God did not spare angels who sinned but cast them into darkness.
Declares that the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and reserve the unrighteous for judgment.
Advises to avoid the way of false teachers, who follow their own desires.
Illustrates the dire state of those who have escaped the corruption of the world but are entangled again.

3.title: Warns that in the last days scoffers will come with mocking words.
Reminds that one day is like a thousand years and vice versa, emphasizing God's timing.
Describes the day of the Lord coming like a thief, bringing destruction.
Urges believers to live holy and godly lives in anticipation of the coming day.
Encourages believers to be diligent to be found by Him without spot or blemish at the coming of Jesus.

1.title: States that God is light and in Him there is no darkness at all.
Emphasizes that walking in the light leads to fellowship with God and others.
Encourages confessing sins to receive forgiveness and cleansing from all unrighteousness.
Warns against claiming to be without sin while still living in darkness.

2.title: Assures believers that if they sin, they have an advocate in Jesus Christ.
Encourages living as Jesus did, walking in love and truth.
States that whoever loves their brother lives in the light, while those who hate remain in darkness.
Warns against loving the world and its desires, which are temporary.

3.title: Highlights the great love God has lavished on us, calling us His children.
Explains that love is demonstrated by laying down one's life for others.
Urges to love not just in words or speech but in actions and truth.
Encourages letting our hearts not be hardened by evil deeds, but to overcome evil with good.

4.title: Calls believers to love one another, for love comes from God.
States that God is made complete in us and our love reflects Him.
Teaches that anyone who confesses Jesus as the Son of God has God’s love.
Highlights that it is impossible to love God and hate a brother simultaneously.

5.title: Declares that everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.
Affirms the victory of Jesus over the world through water and blood.
Assures believers that they have eternal life, providing confidence in their salvation.
Reveals that we have received the glory of the Son of God and know Him.

1.title: John identifies himself as the elder and addresses the chosen lady and her children.
Encourages them to continue walking in truth and love, avoiding evil.
Warns against deceivers who do not acknowledge Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh.
Affirms that those who abide by God's teaching have the assurance of eternal life.
Declares that no one who loves the truth will be condemned.
John greets Gaius, whom he loves in the truth.
Commends Gaius for walking in the truth and showing hospitality to Christian workers.
Acknowledges Diotrephes, who loves to be first and does not acknowledge John's authority.
States that if Diotrephes does not welcome other believers, he will not be welcomed by John.
Commends Demetrius to the church, highlighting his good testimony and integrity.
Urges believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints.
Warns against false teachers who secretly slip in, distorting the grace of God into a license for immorality.
Reminds of past judgments on ungodly people, urging not to forget God’s mercy.
Compares false teachers to rebellious angels, Sodom and Gomorrah, Cain, and Korah.
Encourages believers to build themselves up in their most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.
Exhorts to keep themselves in God’s love, waiting for the mercy of Jesus Christ to bring eternal life.
Concludes with a doxology praising God’s ability to keep believers from stumbling and present them blameless before His glory.
Blesses those who read and hear the prophecy, emphasizing its importance for understanding future events.
Proclaims the return of Jesus Christ, visible to all, including those who pierced Him.
John falls at Jesus' feet in awe, but Jesus reassures him and instructs him to write what he sees.

2.title: Commends the Ephesian church for their hard work and perseverance, yet warns against losing their first love.
Encourages faithfulness even to the point of death, promising the crown of life.

3.title: Addresses the Sardis church, calling them to wake up and strengthen what remains.
Promises the white garments and the name of a new creation to those who are faithful.
Illustrates Jesus standing at the door and knocking, inviting fellowship with those who hear Him.

4.title: John is invited to come up and see the voice speaking, revealing a vision of God's throne.
Describes the four living creatures around the throne, continuously praising God day and night.

5.title: Proclaims that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has triumphed and is worthy to open the scroll.
Heavenly beings praise the Lamb who was slain, declaring His worthiness to receive power and wealth.

6.title: Introduces the opening of the first seal, revealing a white horse and its rider symbolizing conquest.
Describes cosmic disturbances as the sixth seal is opened, signaling significant upheaval.

7.title: Commands the sealing of 144,000 from the tribes of Israel to protect them from divine judgments.
Reveals a great multitude from every nation, standing before the throne and the Lamb in worship.

8.title: Describes an angel offering incense with the prayers of the saints on the golden altar before the throne.
Introduces the seven trumpets, signaling the beginning of a series of judgments.

9.title: Unleashes the first woe with the fifth trumpet, releasing locusts with the power to torment.
Introduces the sixth woe as four angels bound at the Euphrates are released to kill a third of mankind.

10.title: Shows a mighty angel with a rainbow above, holding a little scroll open in his hand.
Commands John to eat the scroll, symbolizing the bittersweet nature of prophetic revelation.

11.title: Appoints two witnesses with the power to prophesy, perform miracles, and face persecution.
Proclaims the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of Christ, marked by the seventh trumpet.

12.title: Depicts a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars.
Describes the war in heaven where Michael and his angels fight against the dragon and his forces.

13.title: Introduces the first beast rising from the sea, given authority and worship from the inhabitants of the earth.
Describes the mark of the beast, requiring everyone to receive a mark on their right hand or forehead.

14.title: Shows the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who have His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads.
Introduces the everlasting gospel being preached to every nation, tribe, language, and people.

15.title: Proclaims the victorious song of Moses and the Lamb, acknowledging God's righteous judgments.
Describes the angels preparing to pour out the seven plagues of God's wrath.

16.title: Outlines the pouring of the first bowl, resulting in painful sores on those with the mark of the beast.
Describes the final judgment with great earthquakes and the destruction of Babylon the Great.

17.title: Introduces the judgment of the great prostitute Babylon, symbolizing widespread corruption and immorality.
Reveals the name written on the prostitute's forehead: 'Mystery, Babylon the Great, the Mother of Prostitutes and of the Abominations of the Earth.'

18.title: Proclaims the fall of Babylon, declaring it has become a dwelling for demons and a haunt for every unclean spirit.
Describes the complete destruction of Babylon with no survivors.

19.title: Depicts Jesus as a rider on a white horse, leading the armies of heaven with justice and truth.
Reveals the name written on Jesus' robe and thigh: 'King of Kings and Lord of Lords.'

20.title: Describes the binding of Satan for a thousand years to prevent deception in the world.
Introduces the Great White Throne judgment, where the dead are judged according to their deeds.

21.title: Vision shifts to cosmic renewal: a new creation succeeds the old, even the sea gone.
Promises God will wipe away every tear, and there will be no more death, mourning, crying, or pain.

22.title: Describes the river of the water of life flowing from God's throne, with the tree of life on its banks.
Jesus declares He is coming soon, urging readiness and faithfulness.
Concludes with a blessing of grace, inviting those who are victorious to come and take the water of life freely.

1.title: Introduces Tobit, a righteous Israelite living in Nineveh, who performs acts of charity and follows God's commandments.
Describes Tobit's blindness as a punishment for his charity towards the poor, highlighting the theme of suffering for righteousness.
Tobit prays for death, expressing his despair and the human struggle with suffering despite faithfulness to God.

2.title: Tobit continues his acts of charity, burying the dead and giving alms, demonstrating unwavering faith and generosity.
Emphasizes Tobit's commitment to righteousness, even in exile, serving as an example of steadfast faith.

3.title: Tobit prays for mercy and deliverance from his afflictions, showing his reliance on divine intervention.
Tobit receives guidance through a vision, instructing him to send his son Tobias on a journey for a safe marriage.

4.title: Tobit advises Tobias to walk in righteousness, avoid sin, and perform acts of charity, reinforcing moral and ethical living.
Encourages Tobias to maintain faith and trust in God’s providence throughout his journey.

5.title: Tobias prepares for his journey, demonstrating obedience to his father's instructions and reliance on divine protection.
Introduces Sarah, Tobias's future wife, who has been afflicted by a demon, setting the stage for divine intervention.

6.title: Tobias encounters Raphael in disguise, who guides him and provides wisdom for his journey.
Raphael advises Tobias on how to overcome the demon and ensure a successful marriage with Sarah.

7.title: Describes the marriage ceremony of Tobias and Sarah, symbolizing the triumph of faith and divine intervention over evil.
Highlights the fulfillment of God’s promise as Tobias and Sarah begin their life together under Raphael’s protection.

8.title: Tobias and Sarah live happily, practicing righteousness and gratitude towards God for their blessings.
Illustrates the harmony and prosperity that result from living in accordance with God’s will.

9.title: Raphael reveals himself as an angel sent by God to guide and protect Tobias, emphasizing divine providence.
Explains the purpose of Raphael’s mission, highlighting the importance of faith and obedience.

10.title: Tobit and Tobias return to Nineveh safely, bringing back wealth and blessings, demonstrating the rewards of faithfulness.
Tobit praises God for His mercy and the successful outcome of their journey, reinforcing themes of gratitude and divine favor.

11.title: Tobit shares his experiences and the lessons learned from Raphael, encouraging others to remain steadfast in faith.
Emphasizes the importance of prayer, charity, and righteousness in overcoming personal and communal challenges.

12.title: Tobit advises future generations to uphold righteousness and maintain their trust in God’s guidance.
Reiterates the blessings that come from living a life of faith, charity, and obedience to God.

13.title: Tobit recounts the blessings and fulfillment that resulted from his and Tobias’s faithful actions.
Concludes with Tobit’s final blessings and prayers for prosperity and righteousness among his descendants.

14.title: Raphael fully reveals his identity as an angel of God, explaining his role in Tobit and Tobias’s lives.
Raphael departs, returning to heaven after ensuring that Tobit and Tobias have fulfilled their divine missions.

1.title: Introduces Judith, a devout and courageous widow from the tribe of Benjamin, who is deeply respected in her community.
Describes Judith’s decision to intervene and save her people from the Assyrian threat, demonstrating her bravery and faith.

2.title: Depicts the Assyrian general Holofernes besieging the city of Bethulia, causing widespread fear and despair among the Israelites.
Judith prays for guidance and strength, committing herself to God’s will as she devises a plan to deliver her people.

3.title: Shows the people of Bethulia losing hope and considering surrender, but Judith remains steadfast in her belief that God will save them.
Judith encourages the people to trust in God and promises to take decisive action against the enemy.

4.title: Describes Judith’s preparation for her mission, including her modest attire to gain the trust of the enemy.
Highlights Judith’s courage as she sets out alone to confront Holofernes, relying on her faith and wisdom.

5.title: Judith successfully gains entrance to Holofernes’ camp by presenting herself as a deserter seeking mercy.
Holofernes is captivated by Judith’s beauty and grace, lowering his guard and allowing her access to his tent.

6.title: Judith engages Holofernes in conversation, earning his trust and securing a place of honor within the camp.
Through her interaction, Judith observes Holofernes’ weaknesses and gathers information critical to her plan.

7.title: Describes the lavish feast where Holofernes indulges, providing Judith the opportunity to execute her plan.
Judith remains composed and faithful, preparing to fulfill her mission at the right moment.

8.title: Judith waits for the perfect moment during the banquet when Holofernes is inebriated and vulnerable.
She seizes the opportunity to behead Holofernes, effectively eliminating the Assyrian threat.

9.title: Judith triumphantly returns to Bethulia with Holofernes’ head, receiving immense gratitude and admiration from her people.
The Israelites celebrate their deliverance, recognizing Judith’s faith and bravery as the catalyst for their salvation.

10.title: Highlights the renewed faith and unity among the Israelites, inspired by Judith’s actions and God’s deliverance.
Judith leads the people in worship and thanksgiving, reinforcing their commitment to God.

11.title: Describes Judith’s ongoing role as a leader and spiritual guide for her people, ensuring their continued prosperity.
She advises the Israelites to remain vigilant and faithful, safeguarding their community against future threats.

12.title: Depicts the flourishing of Bethulia under Judith’s leadership, with peace and prosperity restored.
Judith’s legacy is celebrated, and her story serves as an enduring example of faith, courage, and divine providence.

13.title: Judith blesses her people and prays for their continued faithfulness to God.
Her final blessings emphasize the importance of righteousness and reliance on God for future generations.

14.title: Reflects on the historical significance of Judith’s actions, highlighting the turning point for the Israelites.
Encourages future generations to emulate Judith’s faith and bravery in the face of adversity.

15.title: Judith offers a prayer of thanksgiving, acknowledging God’s role in her success and the salvation of her people.
Her prayer underscores the themes of divine intervention and the rewards of steadfast faith.

16.title: Judith provides final instructions to the Israelites, urging them to maintain their devotion and moral integrity.
Concludes with a benediction, blessing the people and reaffirming their commitment to God’s covenant.

1.title: Explains that wisdom is the principal thing and that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Describes how ungodly people turn away from the Lord and are led astray by their own desires.
Warns against idolatry, highlighting the futility of worshiping created things instead of the Creator.

2.title: Urges individuals to turn away from wickedness and seek righteousness through the fear of the Lord.
