Emphasizes that wisdom comes from God and those who seek it will find true understanding.
Contrasts the fleeting pleasures of the wicked with the enduring rewards of the righteous.

3.title: Affirms that the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them.
Describes the righteous as shining like stars in a dark world, bringing light and guidance.
Promises that the righteous will dwell forever in the presence of the Lord, enjoying eternal peace.

4.title: Highlights the wickedness of idolaters and their disregard for true wisdom.
Warns that those who reject wisdom will face destruction and divine judgment.
Declares that the ungodly will perish and their works will be forgotten, unlike the lasting legacy of the righteous.

5.title: Celebrates wisdom's presence during the creation of the world, guiding all things by her counsel.
Explains that wisdom was the craftsman and agent of God's will in bringing order to the universe.
States that wisdom rejoices in the righteousness of those who seek her and aids them in their endeavors.

6.title: Contrasts the wisdom of God with the foolishness of those who ignore divine guidance.
Describes the consequences of rejecting wisdom, leading to moral decay and societal collapse.
Encourages adherence to wisdom to avoid the pitfalls of folly and ensure a prosperous life.

7.title: Connects wisdom with justice, asserting that true wisdom leads to just actions and decisions.
Emphasizes that wisdom is free and accessible to all who seek her, regardless of social status.
Highlights the importance of mercy and kindness as expressions of wisdom in human interactions.

8.title: Lists the benefits of wisdom, including peace, joy, and the protection of the righteous.
Explains that wisdom provides guidance in times of uncertainty and leads individuals away from evil.
Assures that wisdom will never abandon those who hold her dear, offering constant support and strength.

9.title: Declares that the wisdom of God is beyond human comprehension and cannot be fully grasped.
Encourages humility and reverence before God, recognizing the limits of human understanding.
Affirms that God's wisdom orchestrates all events for the ultimate good of the righteous.

10.title: Illustrates the power of wisdom in overcoming adversity and leading a virtuous life.
Describes wisdom as a shield that protects believers from the snares of evil.
Highlights that wisdom empowers individuals to make righteous choices and avoid temptation.

11.title: Explains that wise governance leads to a just and orderly society, benefiting all its members.
Warns against leaders who lack wisdom, resulting in oppression and chaos.
Encourages rulers to seek wisdom to govern effectively and uphold justice.

12.title: Promises that those who embrace wisdom will be rewarded with honor and lasting prosperity.
Assures that wisdom brings happiness and fulfillment to those who follow her path.
Concludes that the pursuit of wisdom leads to a life of virtue, peace, and divine favor.

13.title: Connects wisdom with the pursuit of immortality, emphasizing the eternal value of righteous living.
Explains that wisdom leads to the soul's immortality through righteous deeds and divine favor.
Encourages believers to seek wisdom as a means to attain eternal life and avoid spiritual death.

14.title: Describes wisdom as a guardian that protects the righteous from the attacks of evil.
Affirms that wisdom shields believers from the consequences of their own and others' wrongdoing.
Highlights that wisdom's protection extends beyond the individual to the community, fostering collective well-being.

15.title: Declares that wisdom is eternal and unchanging, unlike the fleeting nature of human life.
Emphasizes that wisdom endures beyond physical death, offering eternal guidance and support.
Affirms that wisdom's influence persists, ensuring the righteous are remembered and honored forever.

16.title: Explains that wisdom plays a crucial role in divine judgment, ensuring that justice is served.
Highlights that wisdom discerns the true intentions of individuals, determining their fate accordingly.
Encourages believers to trust in wisdom's judgment, knowing that it is fair and righteous.

17.title: Connects humility with wisdom, asserting that the truly wise are humble and seek God's guidance.
Describes how humility opens the heart to receive wisdom and divine favor.
Encourages believers to cultivate humility to fully embrace the benefits of wisdom.

18.title: Illustrates how wisdom positively influences every aspect of life, from personal relationships to societal structures.
Explains that wisdom fosters harmony and understanding, preventing conflicts and discord.
Affirms that wisdom's influence leads to a life of purpose, meaning, and divine alignment.

19.title: Declares that wisdom will ultimately triumph over folly, ensuring the righteous are upheld.
Describes the eternal peace and prosperity that wisdom brings to those who embrace her.
Concludes with a proclamation of wisdom's eternal reign, guiding the righteous into everlasting glory.

1.title: Declares wisdom as a divine gift from God, essential for living a righteous life.
Encourages seeking wisdom early in life, emphasizing its value over riches and power.
Warns against rejecting wisdom, highlighting the consequences of ignorance and folly.

2.title: Explains that wisdom was present at creation and sustains the universe.
Describes the rewards of living wisely, including honor and peace.
Highlights that wisdom protects individuals from harm and guides them in righteousness.

3.title: Urges the righteous to maintain their integrity and avoid corruption.
Encourages generosity and kindness, promising divine blessings in return.
Warns against pride and arrogance, advocating for humility and gratitude.

4.title: Defines true friendship as one that is based on mutual respect and righteousness.
Advises selecting friends wisely, as they influence one's character and actions.
Highlights the benefits of loyal friendships, including support and companionship.

5.title: Emphasizes the power of words, urging restraint and thoughtful speech.
Warns against gossip and slander, promoting honesty and integrity.
Encourages speaking truthfully and kindly, fostering harmonious relationships.

6.title: Warns that excessive love for money can lead to moral decay and spiritual downfall.
Highlights the fleeting nature of wealth compared to the lasting value of wisdom.
Advises using wealth responsibly and generously to benefit others and honor God.

7.title: Praises the virtues of hard work and perseverance in achieving success.
Encourages diligence in one's duties, ensuring reliability and trustworthiness.
Warns against laziness, emphasizing the importance of consistent effort.

8.title: Advocates for the importance of education in cultivating wisdom and virtue.
Describes the benefits of a good education, including moral guidance and intellectual growth.
Encourages lifelong learning and the continuous pursuit of knowledge.

9.title: Defines righteous leadership as one that is just, compassionate, and wise.
Warns against corrupt leaders who abuse their power for personal gain.
Highlights the rewards of serving under wise and just rulers, including societal stability.

10.title: Praises humility as a key virtue that leads to wisdom and divine favor.
Encourages humility in interactions with others, fostering respect and cooperation.
Warns against pride, emphasizing that humility attracts blessings while arrogance leads to downfall.

11.title: Advocates for justice and fairness in all dealings, ensuring equitable treatment for all.
Warns against corruption and favoritism, promoting impartiality in judgments.
Highlights the societal benefits of a just and fair community, including peace and prosperity.

12.title: Explains that the fear of the Lord is the foundation of wisdom and righteous living.
Encourages cultivating a respectful and reverent relationship with God.
Describes the fear of the Lord as a protective and guiding force in one's life.

13.title: Emphasizes the importance of sincere and humble prayer in connecting with God.
Encourages persistent prayer, trusting in God's responsiveness and mercy.
Highlights the benefits of prayer, including guidance, comfort, and divine intervention.

14.title: Praises patience as a virtue that fosters resilience and steadfastness in adversity.
Encourages enduring hardships with grace and trust in God's plan.
Warns against impatience, emphasizing that patience leads to long-term rewards.

15.title: Advocates for forgiveness, promoting healing and reconciliation in relationships.
Describes the liberating effects of forgiving others, both spiritually and emotionally.
Encourages extending mercy and compassion, reflecting God's forgiveness towards humanity.

16.title: Highlights self-control as essential for maintaining moral integrity and avoiding temptation.
Encourages mastering one's desires and impulses to lead a disciplined and virtuous life.
Warns against the dangers of indulgence and lack of self-control, promoting moderation.

17.title: Praises generosity as a reflection of wisdom and compassion towards others.
Encourages giving freely to those in need, emphasizing the joy it brings both giver and receiver.
Highlights the lasting impact of generous actions, fostering community and goodwill.

18.title: Emphasizes the importance of honoring and respecting one's parents and family members.
Encourages maintaining strong family bonds through love, support, and mutual respect.
Highlights the societal benefits of strong, virtuous families as the foundation of community.

19.title: Warns against envy, describing it as a destructive emotion that leads to discord and resentment.
Encourages cultivating contentment and gratitude to overcome feelings of envy.
Highlights the benefits of rejoicing in others' successes rather than coveting their possessions.

20.title: Encourages striving for excellence in all endeavors, reflecting one's commitment to wisdom and virtue.
Defines excellence as a manifestation of one's inner character and dedication to righteousness.
Highlights that the pursuit of excellence leads to personal fulfillment and societal advancement.

21.title: Praises integrity as a cornerstone of a righteous and honorable life.
Warns against compromising one's integrity for personal gain or societal pressure.
Encourages maintaining honesty and moral uprightness in all aspects of life.

22.title: Describes humble service as a pathway to spiritual growth and divine favor.
Encourages serving others selflessly, reflecting God's love and compassion.
Highlights the rewards of humble service, including inner peace and societal respect.

23.title: Advocates for modesty in behavior and appearance, promoting dignity and respect.
Encourages humility and simplicity, avoiding vanity and excessive display.
Highlights the spiritual benefits of modest living, fostering inner beauty and grace.

24.title: Emphasizes that wise leadership is essential for the prosperity and stability of a community.
Encourages leaders to seek wisdom and justice, ensuring fair governance.
Warns against leaders who neglect wisdom, leading to corruption and societal decline.

25.title: Praises gratitude as a fundamental virtue that strengthens one's relationship with God and others.
Encourages expressing thankfulness through actions and words, fostering positive relationships.
Highlights the reciprocal nature of gratitude, where giving thanks leads to receiving blessings.

26.title: Warns against greed, describing it as a root of many evils and personal suffering.
Encourages contentment and moderation to overcome the destructive nature of greed.
Highlights the spiritual emptiness that accompanies a life driven by greed and materialism.

27.title: Praises patience as essential for overcoming life's challenges and maintaining faith.
Encourages perseverance in the face of adversity, trusting in God's plan and timing.
Highlights that enduring hardships with patience leads to spiritual growth and resilience.

28.title: Defines ethical behavior as acting in accordance with wisdom and divine commandments.
Encourages maintaining integrity even when faced with moral dilemmas and societal pressures.
Highlights the long-term benefits of ethical living, including personal honor and community trust.

29.title: Emphasizes the efficacy of sincere prayer in seeking God's guidance and intervention.
Encourages persistent supplication, trusting in God's responsiveness and mercy.
Highlights the transformative power of prayer in fostering spiritual growth and divine favor.

30.title: Praises the blessings that come from living a righteous and wise life.
Encourages adherence to wisdom and virtue to receive God's blessings and protection.
Highlights that righteous living leads to lasting happiness and divine approval.

31.title: Summarizes the key virtues of wisdom, including humility, integrity, and generosity.
Encourages continual pursuit of wisdom and righteousness as lifelong endeavors.
Concludes with a call to live virtuously, honoring God through every aspect of life.

1.title: Baruch writes a letter to the exiles in Babylon, urging them to seek the Lord and abandon their idolatrous practices.
Encourages the people to turn back to God, emphasizing that righteousness leads to life and peace.
Warns against the futility of pursuing wealth and honor without God, highlighting the blessings of obedience.

2.title: Confesses the sins of Israel that led to the destruction of Jerusalem and the exile to Babylon.
Reflects on God's justice and the consequences of the people's unfaithfulness and idolatry.
Acknowledges that the current suffering is a result of turning away from God's commandments.

3.title: Baruch prays for mercy on behalf of the exiles, seeking God’s forgiveness and restoration.
Describes wisdom as a divine attribute that guides and protects the righteous, contrasting with folly.
Praises God’s steadfast love and mercy, affirming that wisdom resides with those who fear the Lord.

4.title: Contemplates the nature of God’s justice, asserting that He is righteous and just in all His ways.
Encourages the exiles to remain faithful, trusting that God will ultimately vindicate the righteous.
Emphasizes the importance of maintaining integrity and righteousness despite external hardships.

5.title: Baruch expresses hope for the restoration of Jerusalem and the return of the exiles to their homeland.
Encourages the people to remain steadfast in their faith, assuring them of God’s promise to gather them again.
Concludes with final exhortations to trust in God’s plan and maintain hope for future redemption.

6.title: An attached epistle in Jeremiah's name to the exiles, ridiculing the powerlessness of Babylonian idols and urging the people not to fear them.

1.title: Azariah begins by praising God for His mercy and steadfast love, acknowledging His sovereignty and righteousness.
He expresses gratitude for God's deliverance of the Israelites from their enemies, recognizing His intervention in their lives.
Azariah confesses the sins of the people, admitting their failures to uphold God's commandments and their reliance on their own strength.
He beseeches God for forgiveness, pleading for His mercy to cleanse them from their transgressions and renew their commitment to righteousness.
Azariah prays for divine guidance, asking God to lead them in the paths of justice and truth.
He seeks protection from future adversities, trusting in God's promise to safeguard and bless the faithful.
Azariah reaffirms his faith in God's eternal nature, emphasizing His omnipotence and omnipresence.
He declares his unwavering trust in God's plans, believing that His will prevails over all circumstances.
Azariah vows to uphold God's laws, dedicating himself to a life of virtue and integrity.
He commits to teaching and guiding others in the ways of the Lord, fostering a community grounded in faith and obedience.
Azariah concludes with final supplications, asking for God's continued presence and favor upon the people.
He ends the prayer with heartfelt praise, celebrating God's greatness and expressing hope for His everlasting kingdom.
Introduces Susanna, a beautiful and virtuous woman living in Babylon, renowned for her piety and charitable deeds.
Describes Susanna bathing in her garden, a place of solitude and prayer, reflecting her dedication to God.
Narrates the scheming of two elders who lust after Susanna and conspire to accuse her falsely of adultery to satisfy their desires.

2.title: Introduces Daniel, a young and wise man who becomes aware of the elders' plot against Susanna and decides to intervene.
Details Daniel's strategic approach to interrogating the elders separately, ensuring their testimonies do not align if fabricated.
Highlights the elders' inability to reconcile their conflicting statements, revealing the truth of their deceit and exonerating Susanna.

3.title: Celebrates Susanna's vindication as the truth prevails, showcasing her unwavering faith and integrity throughout the ordeal.
Emphasizes the moral lessons learned from the incident, including the importance of wisdom, justice, and divine protection for the righteous.
Concludes with praise for God’s intervention, affirming that righteousness is ultimately rewarded and evil is exposed and punished.

1.title: Introduces the idol Bel, revered by the Babylonians, and describes the deceitful practices of its priests who falsely claim that Bel consumes the sacrifices left by the people.
Narrates Daniel’s investigation into the idol Bel, where he discovers that the priests secretly consume the offerings by hiding in the Bel’s belly.
Details Daniel’s confrontation with the priests, exposing their fraud and proving that Bel does not consume the sacrifices, leading to their punishment.
Introduces a living dragon worshipped by the Babylonians, symbolizing their misguided beliefs and the futility of idol worship.
Describes Daniel’s challenge to the dragon, demonstrating his unwavering faith in God and rejecting the dragon’s supposed divine power.
Narrates the miraculous demise of the dragon as Daniel prays to God, showcasing divine intervention and the triumph of true faith over false idols.
Introduces Mattathias, a Jewish priest, and his sons who initiate the revolt against the oppressive decrees of Antiochus Epiphanes.
Describes the outbreak of rebellion as Mattathias and his sons refuse to comply with the emperor's orders to abandon Jewish laws and practices.

2.title: Mattathias dies, and his son Judas Maccabeus assumes leadership of the rebellion, inspiring the people with his courage and faith.
Details Judas' strategic victory against Gorgias, reinforcing the strength and determination of the rebel forces.

3.title: Judas Maccabeus leads successful campaigns against Seleucid forces, reclaiming territories and restoring Jewish worship.
Highlights the purification and rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem, marking a significant spiritual and national milestone.

4.title: Describes the defense of Jerusalem against a major Seleucid assault, showcasing the resilience and tactical prowess of Judas and his men.
Judas secures Jerusalem's borders and establishes a period of relative peace, allowing for religious and cultural restoration.

5.title: Details the establishment of religious reforms to ensure the purity and observance of Jewish laws among the people.
Judas oversees the rebuilding of the Temple, ensuring that it is cleansed and dedicated to the worship of Yahweh alone.

6.title: Judas engages in battles to expand and secure Jewish territories, demonstrating both military skill and strategic alliances.
Highlights diplomatic efforts to gain support from neighboring regions, strengthening the rebel's position against Seleucid forces.

7.title: Addresses internal challenges within the rebel ranks, including disputes and the need for strong, unified leadership.
Judas successfully resolves conflicts, reinforcing his authority and the cohesion of the rebel forces.

8.title: Describes strategic marriages and alliances with neighboring leaders to bolster the rebel's support and legitimacy.
Highlights the importance of alliances in sustaining the rebellion and ensuring long-term stability for the Jewish people.

9.title: Judas leads decisive campaigns against Antiochus Eupator, dealing significant blows to the Seleucid military presence.
Emphasizes the strategic victories that weaken Seleucid control and inspire further support for the rebellion.

10.title: Details the establishment of governance structures to manage reclaimed territories and ensure the rule of law.
Judas implements legal reforms to maintain order and justice within the Jewish community, promoting fairness and righteousness.

11.title: Focuses on the strengthening of religious institutions to preserve Jewish traditions and prevent assimilation.
Highlights efforts to educate and train religious leaders, ensuring the continuity of Jewish teachings and practices.

12.title: Describes diplomatic negotiations aimed at securing peace and favorable terms for the Jewish people with neighboring states.
Emphasizes the importance of peaceful relations in maintaining the stability and prosperity of the Jewish nation.

13.title: Judas conducts final military campaigns to eliminate remaining Seleucid threats, ensuring lasting peace and security.
Details the consolidation of power, with Judas establishing a strong and unified Jewish state free from Seleucid oppression.

14.title: Celebrates Judas Maccabeus' achievements in liberating the Jewish people and restoring their faith and culture.
Judas' legacy is solidified as a national hero, inspiring future generations to uphold Jewish traditions and resist oppression.

15.title: Describes the continued efforts to expand and secure Jewish territories, ensuring the longevity of the newly established state.
Highlights the expansion of influence and the spread of Jewish practices beyond Jerusalem, promoting unity and strength.

16.title: Concludes with reflections on the rebellion's success, attributing victories to divine favor and the unwavering faith of the Jewish people.
Emphasizes the importance of remembrance and gratitude for the sacrifices made during the revolt, ensuring that future generations honor their heritage.

1.title: Introduces the purpose of the book: to provide an accurate historical account of the Maccabean revolt and to encourage faithfulness to God.
Emphasizes the importance of divine providence and the rewards of piety and obedience to God's commandments.
Highlights the consequences of turning away from God, including suffering and oppression by foreign powers.

2.title: Narrates the courageous refusal of Eleazar, a faithful Jew, to abandon his beliefs despite threats of death.
Describes Eleazar's steadfastness and ultimate martyrdom, serving as an example of unwavering faith.
Praises Eleazar's devotion, illustrating the virtues of sacrifice and loyalty to God.

3.title: Details the persecution faced by Jason and Ananias for their refusal to worship idols.
Highlights their resilience and courage in the face of torture, remaining true to their faith.
Commends their martyrdom, reinforcing the theme of steadfastness amidst adversity.

4.title: Describes the oppressive policies of Antiochus Epiphanes, including the desecration of the Temple and the persecution of Jews.
Highlights the desecration of the Temple altar, symbolizing the extent of Antiochus's sacrilege.
Emphasizes the widespread suffering and loss of freedom experienced by the Jewish people under Seleucid rule.

5.title: Details the increased persecution and attempts to force Jews to abandon their religious practices.
Narrates the abduction and martyrdom of Jews who resisted assimilation and idolatry.
Praises the courage of those who remained faithful, despite the escalating threats and brutality.

6.title: Introduces Hannah and her seven sons, who are arrested for refusing to worship Greek gods.
Describes their unwavering faith and refusal to comply with idolatrous demands.
Narrates the martyrdom of the seven sons, highlighting their ultimate sacrifice for their beliefs.

7.title: Tells the story of Onias III, a high priest who seeks divine guidance in the face of political turmoil.
Highlights the miraculous intervention of God in delivering Onias III from assassination attempts.
Emphasizes the protection of righteous leaders by divine providence, reinforcing the theme of God's faithfulness.

8.title: Details the emergence of the Maccabean family as leaders in the fight against Seleucid oppression.
Describes Judas Maccabeus' strategic leadership and his role in rallying the Jewish resistance.
Praises the successes of the Maccabees in reclaiming and purifying the Temple, restoring proper worship.

9.title: Narrates the decisive Battle of Beth Zur, where Judas Maccabeus leads the Jewish forces to victory against the Seleucids.
Highlights the strategic brilliance and bravery of Judas, inspiring the Jewish people to continue their fight for freedom.
Emphasizes the significance of the victory in boosting morale and strengthening the resolve of the Jewish rebels.

10.title: Describes the purification and rededication of the desecrated Temple, a pivotal moment in the Maccabean revolt.
Highlights the restoration of proper worship practices, symbolizing the triumph of faith over oppression.
Praises the collective efforts of the Jewish people in reclaiming their sacred space and honoring God.

11.title: Introduces Antiochus Eupator, the successor of Antiochus Epiphanes, and his attempts to undermine the Maccabean revolt.
Details the continued persecution and the challenges faced by the Jewish rebels under Antiochus Eupator's rule.
Emphasizes the resilience and determination of the Maccabees in maintaining their religious and national identity.

12.title: Narrates the siege of Jerusalem by Seleucid forces, testing the city's defenses and the people's faith.
Describes the miraculous events and divine interventions that aid the Jewish defenders during the siege.
Praises the steadfastness of Jerusalem's inhabitants and their unwavering commitment to God amidst adversity.

13.title: Details the final defeat of Antiochus Eupator by the Maccabean forces, securing Jewish autonomy and religious freedom.
Highlights the restoration of the Temple and the establishment of the Hasmonean dynasty, ensuring lasting peace and prosperity.
Emphasizes the fulfillment of divine promises and the vindication of the Jewish people's faith and perseverance.

14.title: Describes the formal establishment of the Hasmonean Kingdom, marking a new era of Jewish self-governance.
Highlights the political and religious reforms implemented by the Hasmonean rulers to strengthen the nation.
Praises the leadership of the Maccabees in guiding the Jewish people towards stability and continued devotion to God.

15.title: Reflects on the lasting impact of the Maccabean Revolt, emphasizing its significance in Jewish history and identity.
Encourages future generations to remember and honor the sacrifices made by the Maccabees for their faith and freedom.
Concludes with a call to uphold the values of courage, faithfulness, and perseverance demonstrated by the Maccabean leaders.

1.title: Manasseh begins by acknowledging God's greatness and expressing his own unworthiness.
He confesses his numerous sins and acknowledges the severity of his wrongdoing against God and His people.
Manasseh earnestly pleads for God's mercy, recognizing that he deserves punishment but beseeching forgiveness.
He appeals to God's compassion, emphasizing His willingness to forgive and restore those who repent.
Manasseh vows to turn away from his sins and commit to following God's commandments wholeheartedly.
He promises to lead a life of righteousness, humility, and dedicated service to God and His people.
Manasseh concludes with a heartfelt thanksgiving to God for His mercy and the assurance of redemption.
Introduces King Cyrus of Persia issuing a decree allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple.
Describes the return of Zerubbabel and Jeshua to Jerusalem, leading the first group of exiles back to their homeland.
Highlights the laying of the foundation of the Temple and the initial efforts to restore proper worship.

2.title: Narrates the progress of the Temple's reconstruction, despite opposition and limited resources.
Describes the dedication of the Temple, with the people celebrating and offering sacrifices as a sign of renewal.
Emphasizes the restoration of religious practices and the reinstitution of the Law, fostering unity among the people.

3.title: Details the selection and ordination of priests and Levites to serve in the rebuilt Temple, ensuring proper rituals.
Highlights the commitment of the new priests to uphold the Law and maintain the sanctity of the Temple.
Describes the establishment of regular sacrifices and offerings, reinstating the religious life of the community.

4.title: Narrates the opposition faced by the builders from surrounding nations, attempting to halt the reconstruction.
Describes strategies employed by Zerubbabel and Jeshua to overcome external threats and continue their work.
Emphasizes the resilience of the Jewish leaders and their unwavering faith in God's support.

5.title: Introduces Ezra the scribe arriving in Jerusalem, bringing with him a copy of the Law of Moses.
Describes Ezra's role in teaching and enforcing the Law among the people, leading to spiritual revival.
Highlights the people's renewed commitment to follow God's commandments, fostering a sense of community and righteousness.

6.title: Narrates the completion of the Temple, marked by a grand celebration and offerings to God.
Describes the joy and gratitude of the Jewish people for the successful rebuilding, attributing it to divine favor.
Emphasizes the importance of maintaining the sanctity of the Temple and continuing the observance of the Law.

7.title: Details the implementation of religious reforms to purify the community from idolatry and pagan practices.
Describes the establishment of strict observance of dietary laws and Sabbath regulations, ensuring holiness.
Highlights the role of leaders like Ezra in guiding the people towards a life of piety and adherence to God's will.

8.title: Narrates Ezra's efforts to renew the covenant with God, reinforcing the people's dedication to the Law.
Describes the public reading and explanation of the Law, leading to widespread repentance and commitment.
Emphasizes the transformation of the community through Ezra's reforms, fostering unity and righteousness.

9.title: The people confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors, acknowledging their failures to uphold the Law.
They appeal to God's mercy, seeking forgiveness and restoration for their transgressions.
Highlights the communal repentance and the desire to return to a faithful and obedient relationship with God.

10.title: Zerubbabel and Jeshua issue final exhortations to the people, urging continued faithfulness and obedience.
Describes the people's commitment to maintain the practices established by Ezra and the leaders.
Concludes the book with blessings upon the community and a reaffirmation of their dedication to God's Law.

1.title: The author explains his purpose in recounting the events of the Maccabean revolt to provide comfort and understanding.
Expresses deep distress and confusion over the suffering and turmoil faced by the Jewish people.
Seeks divine guidance to comprehend the reasons behind their plight and to find hope amidst despair.

2.title: Describes a profound vision in which the author encounters divine beings who offer insights into the human condition.
Highlights the revelation of God's justice and the moral order governing the universe.
Emphasizes the importance of faith and righteousness in aligning with God's will.

3.title: The author engages in a dialogue with the angel Uriel, seeking answers about the existence of evil and suffering.
Uriel explains the purpose of trials and tribulations in refining faith and character.
Concludes with a reaffirmation of God's ultimate plan for redemption and restoration.

4.title: Explores the attributes of divine wisdom and its role in guiding righteous living.
Discusses the relationship between justice and mercy in the administration of divine law.
Encourages the pursuit of wisdom as a means to understand and fulfill God's commandments.

5.title: Narrates prophetic visions that foretell the deliverance of the Jewish people from oppression.
Highlights the fulfillment of prophecies through the actions of faithful leaders and divine intervention.
Emphasizes the certainty of God's promises and the assurance of their eventual realization.

6.title: Describes apocalyptic visions of the end times, detailing the ultimate confrontation between good and evil.
Explains the process of final judgment, where the righteous are rewarded and the wicked are condemned.
Concludes with a message of hope, assuring believers of their eternal salvation and peace in God's presence.

7.title: Encourages the faithful to persevere in their devotion despite ongoing challenges and adversities.
Reiterates the rewards of steadfast faith and the importance of maintaining hope in divine promises.
Calls for collective unity and resilience among the Jewish people to overcome future trials.

1.title: Enoch, a righteous man whose eyes were opened by God, blesses the elect and righteous for a remote generation to come.
The eternal God will tread upon Mount Sinai and appear in strength from the heaven of heavens.
He comes with ten thousands of His holy ones to execute judgment upon all and destroy the ungodly.

6.title: The Watchers, led by Sêmîazâz, descend on Mount Hermon and take human wives to beget children.
Two hundred angels swear an oath together and bind themselves by mutual imprecations to carry out their plan.

7.title: The unions produce giants (Nephilim) whose height was three hundred cubits, who consume all human acquisitions.

8.title: Azâzêl teaches men to make weapons and the art of war, while other angels teach forbidden knowledge.

9.title: Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel appeal to God to judge the inhabitants of the world and the fallen angels.

10.title: God commands the imprisonment of Azâzêl and the binding of the fallen angels for seventy generations.

12.title: Enoch is called to intercede for Azazel and the fallen angels, announcing their first and final doom.

14.title: Enoch is taken up in visions to the throne of the Most High, seeing the crystal palace and God's glory.

15.title: God declares that the spirits of the giants will become evil spirits upon the earth, afflicting mankind.

17.title: Enoch is taken on journeys through the earth and Sheol, seeing the places of punishment and blessing.

18.title: He sees the prison of the stars and angels who transgressed God's commandments.

20.title: The names and functions of the seven archangels are revealed: Uriel, Raphael, Raguel, Michael, Saraqael, Gabriel, and Remiel.

21.title: Enoch visits the preliminary and final places of punishment for the fallen angels.

22.title: He sees Sheol with its divisions for the righteous and wicked dead, awaiting final judgment.

24.title: The Tree of Life is shown, whose fruit will be given to the elect for eternal life.

27.title: The accursed valley is revealed where the final judgment will take place.

36.title: Enoch completes his journey to the four corners of the earth, seeing all the portals of heaven.

2.title: Enoch contemplates the unchanging order of sun, moon, and stars as a witness to God's faithful governance.

3.title: The trees obey their seasons except for the few evergreens — a parable of the unfaithful and the faithful.

4.title: The summer's burning heat is set as another reminder that creation moves only by God's appointment.

5.title: All creation obeys its appointed law, but mankind has transgressed; therefore the curse falls and the elect alone are spared.

11.title: When the earth is purged, God will pour out the storehouses of blessing, and truth and peace will reign.

13.title: Enoch announces to Azazel and the others their judgement; the Watchers ask him to write a petition for forgiveness on their behalf.

16.title: The spirits that came forth from the giants will continue to corrupt the earth until the day of the great consummation.

19.title: Uriel shows Enoch where the Watchers stand who led mankind into idolatry, and tells him their judgement is fixed.

23.title: At the western edge of the world Enoch sees a stream of fire that never pauses — the source of the lights of heaven.

25.title: Michael tells Enoch that the fragrant tree will be transplanted to the holy place after the judgement and given to the righteous as food.

26.title: Enoch sees the holy mountain at the center of the earth and the accursed valley beside it.

28.title: Enoch travels eastward into a wilderness of trees and finds a stream that flows continually.

29.title: Enoch sees trees that exhale frankincense and myrrh — the source of the fragrances of paradise.

30.title: Beyond the first valley Enoch finds another with mastic-like trees and waters running through it.

31.title: Mountains in the east yield nectar, galbanum, and other costly substances that anoint the inhabited world.

32.title: Enoch sees the eastern paradise where the trees of choice spices grow, and learns it was the Garden of Righteousness.

33.title: At the eastern edge of the earth Enoch beholds great beasts and birds in their varied kinds, each one lovely in voice and form.

34.title: Enoch travels to the north and is shown the three open portals from which the cold winds and frost go forth.

35.title: At the west he finds three portals like those in the east, perfectly mirroring the heavenly order.

37.title: Enoch begins the second vision, the vision of wisdom, lifting up his voice to speak words of the Holy One.
Three Parables are imparted to Enoch according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits.

38.title: The first parable concerns the coming judgment of the wicked and the congregation of the righteous.

39.title: The abode of the righteous and the Elect One is revealed, with praises of the blessed.

40.title: The four archangels are presented: Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Phanuel.

42.title: Wisdom finds no dwelling place on earth and returns to heaven, while unrighteousness flows like water.

46.title: The Ancient of Days and the Son of Man appear, whose face was full of graciousness like a holy angel.
This Son of Man will raise up kings from their seats and break the teeth of sinners.

45.title: The Elect One sits on the throne of glory to judge the works of the holy ones in heaven.

48.title: The Son of Man is the fount of righteousness, the stay of the righteous, and light of the Gentiles.

51.title: The resurrection of the dead and separation of the righteous and wicked by the Judge is described.

52.title: The six metal mountains represent different periods of earthly dominion before the Elect One's reign.

54.title: The valley of judgment and the angels of punishment are revealed to execute final justice.

58.title: The blessedness of the saints who will inherit the new earth is proclaimed.

60.title: Behemoth and Leviathan, the great sea and land monsters, are described in their appointed places.

61.title: Angels measure Paradise while the Elect One judges the righteous and praises God.

62.title: The mighty kings will see the Elect One sitting on the throne of glory in their final judgment.

69.title: The secret oath by which the forces of nature are bound is revealed to Enoch.

41.title: Enoch sees how human deeds are weighed in a balance and how the houses of the elect and the houses of sinners are kept apart.

43.title: The stars are likened to the souls of the holy, each weighed and named according to its faithfulness.

44.title: A brief vision of stars whose form is changed; they become flashes of lightning bound to a new course.

47.title: The prayers of the righteous and the cry of their blood ascend to the Lord of Spirits, and the books are opened for judgement.

49.title: Wisdom is poured out on the Elect One, the spirit of insight rests upon him, and his glory shall not fail.

50.title: A change is announced for the holy and elect; even sinners are offered repentance before the appointed day.

53.title: A deep valley with open mouths is prepared for the kings and mighty who oppress the elect.

55.title: The Lord of Spirits swears never again to destroy the earth as in the Flood, and seats the Elect One upon the throne of his glory.

56.title: The angels of punishment go forth with their scourges, and the kings of the east set themselves in motion against Israel.

57.title: A great host comes riding in chariots from the east, west, and south as a sign of the gathering of the nations for judgement.

59.title: A short interlude on the secrets of lightning and thunder, which serve either as blessing or as judgement at God's command.

63.title: The condemned kings plead for a moment's respite to confess and worship the Lord of Spirits, but their petition is denied.

64.title: Enoch is shown the angels who descended and seduced mankind, now bound and held under judgement.

65.title: Noah, seeing the earth trembling toward destruction, hurries to the ends of the earth to call upon his great-grandfather Enoch.

66.title: Enoch is shown the angels of punishment readying the subterranean waters to be unleashed upon the earth.

67.title: God speaks to Noah, declaring his lot blameless; the angels begin building the wooden ark for him.

68.title: Enoch hands on to Methuselah the secrets contained in the Parables and the names of the angels he has seen.

70.title: Enoch's name is lifted from the earth to be among the heavenly beings around the Lord of Spirits.

71.title: Enoch is taken up in spirit, sees the throne and the holy ones, and is hailed as the Son of Man born to righteousness.

72.title: The book of the courses of the heavenly luminaries begins, revealed to Enoch by the angel Uriel.
The sun travels through six portals in the east and six in the west, determining seasons and years.
The solar year consists of 364 days, maintaining perfect order in its appointed times.

73.title: The moon's course and phases are described, with its waxing and waning in precise cycles.
The moon borrows its light from the sun and travels through the same portals.

74.title: The lunar year of 354 days is compared to the solar year, showing the discrepancy.
The calendar ensures that festivals occur on the correct days according to divine ordinance.

76.title: The twelve winds and their portals are described, bringing different weather patterns.

77.title: The four quarters of the world are mapped with seven mountains, rivers, and islands.

78.title: The sun and moon maintain their appointed courses without transgression.

80.title: In the days of sinners, the cosmic order will be perverted due to human wickedness.
The luminaries will change their courses, leading to confusion and calamity on earth.

81.title: Enoch sees the heavenly tablets containing all the deeds of mankind throughout generations.

82.title: Enoch is charged to teach his son Methuselah about the cosmic order and calendar.
The four intercalary days are established to maintain the perfect 364-day year.

75.title: The leaders of thousands among the host of heaven preside over the four intercalary days that complete the solar year of 364.

79.title: Uriel's full disclosure of every star and luminary's law is brought to a close, leaving Enoch with the complete order of the heavens.

83.title: Enoch tells his son Methuselah about visions he has seen before taking a wife.
He sees the earth tilting and being destroyed, causing him great distress and prayer.

84.title: God responds to Enoch's prayer, revealing that judgment will come upon the earth for its corruption.

85.title: The history of the world is revealed through symbolic animals, beginning with Adam as a white bull.

86.title: The fall of the Watchers is depicted as stars falling from heaven and corrupting the earth.

87.title: The seven archangels come to execute judgment upon the fallen angels and their offspring.

89.title: Noah's flood cleanses the earth, with Noah represented as a white bull who survives the deluge.
The post-flood world sees the emergence of different nations represented by various animals.
The Exodus and wilderness period are depicted with sheep being led by a ram (Moses).
The judges and kings of Israel are shown as rams and sheep leading the flock.
The divided kingdom and eventual destruction of Jerusalem by foreign beasts is portrayed.
The Babylonian exile and return under Cyrus are represented by foreign shepherds.

90.title: The Maccabean revolt is depicted as a great horn growing among the sheep to fight the oppressors.
The final judgment sees all the beasts and birds gathered for destruction.
The new Jerusalem descends, and all nations are converted, with the Messiah appearing as a white bull.

88.title: One of the four binds the first fallen star and casts it into a narrow, dark abyss — the prison of the Watchers.

91.title: Enoch calls his children to gather and listen to his words of admonition for the last days.
The Apocalypse of Weeks begins, dividing history into ten periods or 'weeks'.
In the eighth week, the righteous will acquire houses through their righteousness.

92.title: Enoch writes his book of admonition for his children and all who will live in the last days.

93.title: The first seven weeks cover from Adam to the building of the Temple and its destruction.
In the seventh week, an apostate generation will arise, and many evil deeds will be done.
After the seventh week, the eighth week of righteousness will come with judgment.

94.title: Woes are pronounced upon sinners who build their houses with sin and oppression.

95.title: Enoch grieves over the sinners but encourages the righteous to persevere.

96.title: The righteous are given grounds for hope while the wicked face divine judgment.

100.title: The sinners will destroy each other, but the righteous will be safe in divine protection.

102.title: The different destinies of the righteous and sinners in the afterlife are contrasted.

104.title: The righteous are assured they will shine as lights of heaven and have great joy.

105.title: God and the Messiah will dwell with mankind in the new creation.

106.title: Noah is born with supernatural appearance, causing fear and wonder in his father Lamech.
Enoch explains that Noah will be preserved through the coming flood to repopulate the earth.

107.title: The continuing cycle of transgression and righteousness throughout human generations is revealed.

108.title: Enoch writes a final book for those who keep the law in the last days.
The place of punishment for sinners and blasphemers is described as a chaotic wilderness of fire.
The spirits of the righteous who suffered for God will be transformed and given honor.
The final separation between the righteous and wicked is accomplished for eternity.

97.title: The wealthy and the cruel are reminded that no riches can purchase deliverance in the day of the great judgement.

98.title: Enoch swears to wise and foolish alike that the earth will be made witness against them and their secret sins will be exposed.

99.title: Woes are pronounced upon those who alter the words of righteousness, who fashion idols, and who revile what is holy.

101.title: Heaven and earth themselves obey the Most High; how much more should the children of heaven fear and serve him.

103.title: Enoch swears by the heavenly tablets that the souls of the righteous are kept in joy, contrary to all that the world supposes.

1.title: The 'Two Ways' framework introduced — the way of life summarized as love of God, love of neighbor, and radical generosity toward enemies.

2.title: An expanded decalogue: the prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft, magic, abortion, false speech, and double-mindedness.

3.title: Pastoral warnings against the small habits — anger, lust, omens, lies, murmuring — that grow into the great sins.

4.title: Practical instructions on honoring teachers, sharing possessions, training children, and the mutual duties of slaves and masters.

5.title: A comprehensive list of the vices and dispositions that mark the way of death; readers are urged to escape from them.

6.title: Closing exhortation to the moral teaching; permission for varied observance levels, but a firm warning against meat sacrificed to idols.

7.title: Practical instructions for baptism: the trinitarian formula, preferred forms of water, and the fast that precedes the rite.

8.title: Distinguishes Christian fasting and prayer from contemporary practice; appoints Wednesday and Friday fasts and the Lord's Prayer thrice daily.

9.title: The earliest known Eucharistic liturgy: prayers over the cup and the broken bread, with the rule that only the baptized may receive.

10.title: The post-communion thanksgiving: praise for God's care of the Church and a final petition that grace come and the world pass away.

11.title: Tests for traveling teachers, apostles, and prophets — including how long they may stay and what counts as a sign of fraud.

12.title: How to receive Christian travelers: hospitable but not indefinitely, and never supporting the idle who use the faith for gain.

13.title: The provision for resident prophets and teachers, who receive the firstfruits as Israel's priests once did.

14.title: Sunday gathering for thanksgiving and breaking of bread, with reconciliation required before the offering can be pure.

15.title: Appointment of bishops and deacons; manner of reproving fellow believers; their place alongside prophets and teachers.

16.title: Apocalyptic warning to remain watchful: false prophets and the world-deceiver will arise, but those who endure will see the Lord come on the clouds.

1.title: Reuben's deathbed confession of his sin with Bilhah, framed as a warning to his sons against the destructive power of lust.
Simeon repents of his envy toward Joseph and counsels his sons that envy poisons the soul and provokes God's discipline.
Levi recounts heavenly visions of the priestly orders, the coming of the Messianic priest, and the moral demands of the priesthood.
Judah recalls his life of conquest and his fall through wine and the Tamar episode; he charges his sons against drunkenness, greed, and fornication.
Issachar models the simple, hard-working farmer's life and commends to his sons singleness of heart and integrity in labor.
Zebulun, who alone wept over Joseph in the pit, urges his sons to practice compassion and almsgiving as the marks of a righteous life.
Dan repents of his anger and hatred toward Joseph and warns his sons that anger and falsehood open the soul to the spirits of Beliar.
Naphtali instructs his sons to live according to the order God set in nature, with visions warning of Israel's apostasy and restoration.
Gad confesses his hatred of Joseph and traces hatred itself as the root of murder, slander, and ruin; he commends love and forgiveness.
Asher's doctrine of 'two ways': every action springs from one of two minds, and the soul's posture toward good or evil determines its destiny.
Joseph rehearses his trials — the pit, slavery, the Egyptian temptation, prison — as proof that chastity, patience, and forgiveness are vindicated by God.
Benjamin commends the 'pure mind' that sees only good in others, modeling himself on the forgiving Joseph and pointing forward to the Messiah.
Moses receives the prophecy of Israel's coming apostasy and exile, and of the eventual restoration when God will create a new spirit in his people.

2.title: The angel of the presence narrates the six days of creation and the institution of the Sabbath, with each day's works enumerated.

3.title: Adam names the animals, Eve is formed, and the Fall is retold with added detail about Eden's geography and the angels' role.

4.title: The genealogy from Cain and Abel through Seth and Enoch, with extended attention to Enoch's translation and his role as a heavenly scribe.

5.title: The fallen Watchers take human wives, the Nephilim corrupt the earth, and God resolves to bring the Flood; Noah alone finds favor.

6.title: After the Flood, Noah builds an altar and receives a covenant; the feast of weeks and the 364-day calendar are revealed.

7.title: Noah plants a vineyard, drinks of its wine, and divides the earth among his three sons by lot.

8.title: The descendants of Shem are traced and the boundaries of the three sons' inheritances are set out in detail.

9.title: The further subdivision of the earth among the sons of Ham, Shem, and Japheth, with each region named and assigned.

10.title: The unclean spirits begin to lead astray Noah's children; Mastema is permitted to keep a tenth, and angels teach Noah the use of medicines.

11.title: The line of Shem continues; Mastema's idolatry spreads through the nations; Abram is born and even as a child rejects idols.

12.title: Abram challenges his father Terah's idol-making, burns the family idols, and is called by God to leave his country.

13.title: Abram travels through Shechem and Bethel, descends to Egypt, and parts from Lot, who chooses the Jordan plain.

14.title: God appears to Abram in a vision, promises a son and an innumerable seed, and ratifies the covenant by passing between the divided animals.

15.title: God commands circumcision as the sign of his covenant with Abraham and his descendants, with the eighth day fixed as the time.

16.title: The angels visit Abraham at Mamre, announce the birth of Isaac, and bring fire upon Sodom; Isaac is born the following year.

17.title: Isaac is weaned, Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, and Mastema challenges God concerning Abraham's loyalty — setting up the test on Moriah.

18.title: Abraham's faith is tested at Mount Moriah; Isaac is bound on the altar and a ram is provided in his place.

19.title: Sarah dies and is buried at Hebron; Rebekah is brought for Isaac; Abraham instructs and blesses his grandson Jacob.

20.title: Abraham assembles all his sons and grandsons, charges them to keep the way of the LORD, and warns them against intermarriage with the Canaanites.

21.title: Abraham gives his deathbed instructions to Isaac on offerings, blood, and the avoidance of idolatry.

22.title: At the feast of weeks Abraham gives a final blessing to Jacob and dies; he is buried beside Sarah at Hebron.

23.title: The narrator laments how human lifespans have shrunk, and prophesies an end-time restoration when the righteous will live to a great age.

24.title: Isaac digs his father's wells, prospers, and makes a covenant of peace with Abimelech at Beersheba.

25.title: Rebekah summons Jacob and binds him by oath not to take a Canaanite wife, then blesses him with words of prophecy.

26.title: At Rebekah's instigation Jacob takes the blessing intended for Esau, presenting himself before the blind Isaac with goat-skins on his hands.

27.title: Esau plots vengeance, and Rebekah hurries Jacob away to her brother Laban in Haran for safety and a wife.

28.title: Jacob serves Laban for Rachel, is given Leah by deceit, and over twenty years his eleven sons and daughter Dinah are born.

29.title: Jacob slips away from Laban, is overtaken and reconciled, then meets Esau in fearful expectation.

30.title: The defilement of Dinah and the slaughter at Shechem are retold, and a long legal warning against marriage with Gentiles is added.

31.title: Jacob purifies his household and returns to Bethel; Isaac blesses Levi (the priesthood) and Judah (the kingship) above his other grandsons.

32.title: At Bethel Levi is set apart for the eternal priesthood; Jacob tithes; the death of Rachel and the Reuben-Bilhah incident are noted.

33.title: Reuben's sin with Bilhah is retold and used as the occasion for an extended legal prohibition of incestuous unions.

34.title: Jubilees inserts a war between Jacob's sons and the Amorite kings, and then narrates Joseph's betrayal and sale into Egypt.

35.title: Rebekah charges Jacob and Esau to remain at peace with one another, blesses Jacob, and dies; she is buried at Hebron.

36.title: Isaac calls his two sons, divides his goods, charges them to brotherly love, and dies; he is buried with his fathers.

37.title: Esau's sons stir up their father against Jacob over Isaac's blessing; war with hired Edomite forces is prepared.

38.title: Battle is joined at the city gate; Judah strikes down Esau, and the Edomites are placed under tribute to Jacob.

39.title: Joseph rises in Potiphar's house and resists the seduction of his master's wife, and so is cast into prison.

40.title: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of plenty and famine and is set over all Egypt as second only to the king.

41.title: Judah's sons fail to give Tamar offspring, she conceives by Judah himself, and the affair is interpreted as ground for a legal warning.

42.title: The famine drives Jacob's sons to Egypt for grain, where they are accused, tested, and sent home with Simeon held back.

43.title: The hidden cup ruse is played out and Joseph reveals himself to his brothers, weeping over them and providing for the family.

44.title: Jacob sets out for Egypt with his household, offers sacrifices at Beersheba, and is reassured by God in a night vision.

45.title: Joseph receives his father in Egypt and settles the family in Goshen; Joseph manages the famine years for Pharaoh.

46.title: After Jacob's death the Israelites multiply in Egypt, and a new king arises who reduces them to bondage.

47.title: Moses is born under Pharaoh's edict, hidden in the river, raised in the palace, and flees to Midian after killing the Egyptian.

48.title: Moses returns to Egypt at God's call; the plagues fall, Mastema is restrained, and Israel goes out with a high hand.

49.title: An extended legal section on the proper observance of the Passover — its date, the slaughter, the meal, and who may participate.

50.title: The closing chapter sets out the laws of the Sabbath and of the jubilee years, sealing the revelation Moses received on the mount.

1.title: The frame story: God conceives love for the wise Enoch and sends two angels to bring him up to behold the heavenly dwellings.

2.title: Before he is taken away, Enoch warns his sons not to turn from the God who made heaven and earth.

3.title: The angels carry Enoch on their wings to the first heaven, where he beholds the upper waters and the firmament.

4.title: Enoch is presented to the rulers of the stellar orders — two hundred angels who govern the host of heaven.

5.title: Enoch is shown the storehouses of snow and the angels who guard them.

6.title: He sees further treasure-houses of dew and rain, kept by their own attendant angels.

7.title: In the second heaven Enoch sees the prison of the angels who rebelled and now await the great judgement.

8.title: Enoch is shown paradise in the third heaven — the place prepared for the righteous, with rivers of milk, honey, oil, and wine.

9.title: An angel explains that paradise is the inheritance of those who endured offences and walked in righteousness on earth.

10.title: On the northern side of the third heaven Enoch sees a place of cruel torments prepared for the wicked.

11.title: Enoch is taken into the fourth heaven and shown the orderly paths of the sun and moon.

12.title: He sees the strange winged elements of the sun — phoenixes and chalkydri — that escort the daystar through the heavens.

13.title: Enoch is brought to the gates by which the sun rises in its appointed seasons.

14.title: He is shown the corresponding gates in the west by which the sun sets each day of the year.

15.title: At the rising of the sun the phoenixes and chalkydri break forth in song, and all earthly birds answer in their flight.

16.title: Enoch is shown the gates by which the moon enters and leaves heaven through the cycle of the year.

17.title: In the midst of the heavens Enoch sees armed angelic hosts who serve the Lord in unending sacred song.

18.title: In the fifth heaven Enoch finds the Grigori — the Watchers — sorrowing in silence over their fallen brethren.

19.title: Enoch sees seven companies of glorious angels in the sixth heaven, ordering the seasons and the moral life of mankind.

20.title: Reaching the seventh heaven, Enoch sees archangels, dominions, cherubim, and seraphim ranged about the divine throne.

21.title: The six-winged seraphim and the cherubim never depart from the throne, covering it with their wings and singing.

22.title: On Aravoth, the tenth heaven, Enoch sees the face of the Lord like glowing iron and is anointed with oil of glory.

23.title: An archangel teaches Enoch all the works of heaven and earth so that he may write them down for his sons.

24.title: God calls Enoch to sit at his left hand beside Gabriel and prepares to reveal the secret of creation.

25.title: God commands the lower invisible realm to bring forth Adoil, a great light from whose belly all visible creation begins.

26.title: A second invisible being, Archas, comes forth hard from the deep, becoming the foundation of the lower world.

27.title: From light and darkness God forms the waters above and the firmament that divides them.

28.title: God gathers the lower waters together and the chaos becomes dry — the third day of creation in 2 Enoch's voice.

29.title: God forms the heavenly hosts from fire; one of the archangels, Satanail, is cast down for ambition against his Maker.

30.title: On the third day God commands the earth to bring forth herb and tree; paradise is planted and Adam is shaped on the sixth day.

31.title: God places Adam in Eden in the east, charging him to keep the commandment and the testament.

32.title: Earth Adam is, and to earth Adam shall return, but God promises not to destroy him utterly.

33.title: God appoints the eighth day as a sign of the world to come, when the sevens of history are fulfilled.

34.title: Looking down from heaven God grieves over the rejection of his commandments and the rise of idolatry.

35.title: From the seed of the unfaithful God will yet raise up another generation, faithful and discerning.

36.title: God grants Enoch thirty days to return home, gather his household, and pass on the books before being taken up forever.

37.title: Because Enoch's face has been transformed by the divine glory, an icy angel is sent to cool it so men can bear his appearance.

38.title: The Lord commissions the two angels to bring Enoch back to the earth and stand beside him until his term is up.

39.title: Enoch opens his fatherly admonition to his children, charging them to receive the will of the Lord.

40.title: Enoch tells his sons that what he speaks comes from the Lord's own lips, which his eyes have seen from beginning to end.

41.title: He weeps over Adam, Eve, and all who fell into ruin and dishonour through disobedience.

42.title: Enoch describes the serpentine guardians of hell and the contrasting blessedness of paradise.

43.title: Enoch declares that he has measured and written down every deed and every righteous judgement on earth.

44.title: Because every man bears God's likeness, contempt or harm shown to one's neighbor is contempt shown to the Lord himself.

45.title: Offerings made in haste and sincerity are received; God values the heart of the giver more than the size of the gift.

46.title: Enoch calls his people once again to take in the words of his lips with full attention.

47.title: Enoch insists that everything he hands on derives from the Lord's lips and not from his own invention.

48.title: An astronomical interlude on the sun's path through 182 thrones north and south through the year.

49.title: Enoch forbids swearing by heaven, earth, or any creature, anticipating the saying later given by Christ.

50.title: Enoch warns that no work of any man can stay concealed; every act is written in the heavenly books.

51.title: Stretch out your hands to the poor according to your strength — almsgiving is the surest investment with God.

52.title: A series of beatitudes blessing those who praise God, keep peace, judge justly, and refrain from cursing.

53.title: Enoch warns his children that no father can intercede for their sins once they have passed; each soul is accountable for itself.

54.title: The written books of Enoch are entrusted to his children as a permanent inheritance of peace and instruction.

55.title: Enoch tells his children that the day appointed for his removal from the earth has drawn near.

56.title: Methuselah requests that his father bless their dwellings and household before his departure.

57.title: Enoch instructs Methuselah to gather all his brothers and the people for a final farewell address.

58.title: Enoch begins his great farewell discourse on right conduct toward God, neighbor, and beast.

59.title: Cruelty even to animals defiles the soul that does it; the responsibility extends beyond human society.

60.title: He who takes a man's life kills also his own soul; no remedy remains for him in time or eternity.

61.title: Whatever a man wishes for himself from God, that he should do for every living soul — the golden rule in Enoch's voice.

62.title: Blessed is the man who brings his offerings in patience and faith; he shall find pardon and reward.

63.title: When a man clothes the naked and fills the hungry, his recompense is sure with God.

64.title: Hearing that Enoch is to be taken up, the people gather and beg one final word of blessing.

65.title: Enoch summarises God's making of the visible from the invisible and his appointment of times for every creature.

66.title: His parting charge: keep your souls from injustice, walk before the Lord with fear, and serve no other god.

67.title: While the people watch, the Lord sends darkness, and Enoch is borne away by the angels into the highest heaven.

68.title: A closing chronological note: Enoch was born and translated on the same day of the same month, having lived 365 years.

1.title: The opening greeting and a regretful note that internal trouble has prevented Rome from writing sooner.

2.title: Clement recalls the Corinthians' past virtues — their humility, their generosity, their willingness to forgive.

3.title: Once Corinth grew comfortable, jealousy and contention arose, and the unworthy began to rise up against the elders.

4.title: Clement recites a chain of biblical victims of envy — Abel, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David — to show its destructive power.

5.title: Bringing the lesson up to his own generation, Clement names Peter and Paul as having suffered through envy and fought the good fight.

6.title: Many other Christians, including women, have endured cruel deaths in this same generation through envy and persecution.

7.title: Clement reminds his hearers — and himself — that they are all in the same arena and must repent together.

8.title: He cites the prophets and the Lord's own oath that he desires not the death of the sinner but his repentance.

9.title: Enoch was translated for his obedience and Noah preached repentance to the world; both serve as patterns to follow.

10.title: Abraham's repeated obedience — leaving his country, offering Isaac — shows the rewards of faithful obedience.

11.title: Lot's hospitality and godliness preserved him while Sodom perished; his wife stands as a warning against doubting hearts.

12.title: Rahab is held up for her faith in receiving the spies, and the scarlet cord is read as a symbol of redemption by Christ's blood.

13.title: Clement quotes the Beatitudes-style sayings of Jesus on humility and gentleness as the rule for the church's common life.

14.title: He warns that following the schismatic faction means disobeying God himself; the wicked will be cut off from the land.

15.title: Some claim peace with their lips but their hearts are far from God; cleave instead to those who cultivate genuine peace.

16.title: Clement quotes Isaiah 53 at length to show that the Lord himself came in lowliness, not in pomp, as the model for all believers.

17.title: The prophets walked in goat-skins and sheep-skins, despised in the world; their humility is the church's pattern.

18.title: David, the man after God's own heart, prayed in deep repentance — Clement quotes Psalm 51 in full as the model of contrition.

19.title: Clement insists that the chain of humble examples is a moral inheritance for every age, including the present.

20.title: Heavens, sun, moon, stars, seasons, and creatures all move in peaceful order at God's command — a rebuke to human strife.

21.title: Take heed lest the multiplied mercies of God become the ground of our condemnation; walk in love and unity.

22.title: Christ himself addresses the church through the psalms, calling for the fear of the Lord and the love of life.

23.title: The all-merciful Father shows favor to the simple-hearted; Clement warns against double-mindedness and impatience.

24.title: The constant cycle of seed dying and rising, and of day succeeding night, witnesses to the resurrection that Christ has secured.

25.title: Clement appeals to the legendary phoenix of Arabia as a natural sign that God can raise the dead.

26.title: If a single bird is so renewed by God's hand, how much more those who have served him in faith — buttressed with psalm citations.

27.title: He who has commanded us not to lie cannot himself lie; nothing is impossible with him, and our hope is therefore secure.

28.title: Because nothing is hidden from God, we must forsake evil works and live in his sight as those expecting judgment.

29.title: Citing Deuteronomy, Clement reminds the church that they are God's own portion and ought to draw near in holiness.

30.title: As people set apart for God, the Corinthians must shun gossip, drunkenness, and impurity, clothing themselves in unity and humility.

31.title: Look back at the patriarchs: they obtained blessing through faith and obedience, not through their own ambition.

32.title: Priests, Levites, and the Lord himself according to the flesh have come from Abraham — every gift is rooted in his obedience.

33.title: Justification by faith does not free us from good works; the Creator himself models tireless activity for our imitation.

34.title: The diligent worker can look his master in the face; we should be eager and confident in the work appointed to us.

35.title: Clement enumerates the gifts of God — life, righteousness, truth, faith, self-control — that await the obedient.

36.title: Through Christ, the Lord opens the heights of heaven to us; Clement quotes Hebrews-style passages on his high-priestly ministry.

37.title: Drawing on military discipline, Clement urges that every member fulfill his rank and follow the order set down by the commander.

38.title: Strong and weak, rich and poor, wise and ignorant — each has need of the other and ought to give thanks for the other.

39.title: Citing Job 4, Clement mocks the proud who exalt themselves; their boasting is destroyed in a moment by the Lord.

40.title: God has fixed times, seasons, and orders for sacrifice and service; we must do all things in the order he has appointed.

41.title: In Israel sacrifices were offered only at the appointed place by the appointed persons; the church's worship needs the same order.

42.title: Christ was sent by God, the apostles by Christ, and the apostles in turn appointed bishops and deacons in every place.

43.title: As God settled the priesthood by the budding of Aaron's rod, so the apostles arranged the orderly succession of ministers.

44.title: Clement's central charge: the apostles foresaw strife about the office and provided rules; deposing blameless presbyters is grave sin.

45.title: Daniel and the three young men suffered at the hands of the godless, but God vindicated them; the Corinthian rebels mirror the persecutors.

46.title: Scripture teaches us to attach ourselves to the holy; one schism in the body wounds the entire body of Christ.

47.title: Clement reminds the Corinthians that even in Paul's day they were given to factions; they should be ashamed to repeat the sin.

48.title: Let the Corinthians fall down before the Lord with tears and beg his mercy; the gates of righteousness stand open to repentance.

49.title: Clement begins his hymn to love — love that bears all things, love which the saints have always borne and through which the saints are perfected.

50.title: He continues praising love as the only sufficient cover for sin; only those gathered into love will be made manifest in the kingdom.

51.title: Implore forgiveness for past faults; the leaders of sedition should consider the common hope rather than their own pride.

52.title: The Lord requires no sacrifice but a heart confessing — quotation of the psalms on the offering of thanksgiving.

53.title: When Israel sinned at Sinai, Moses begged that his own name be blotted out so the people might be spared — the perfect picture of selfless love.

54.title: Clement appeals: let any noble Christian whose presence has caused contention voluntarily withdraw, that the body may be at peace.

55.title: Even pagan kings and women like Esther and Judith have laid down their lives for their people — Christians ought to do no less.

56.title: Pray for those who have stumbled into sin that they may receive correction with meekness from God's hand.

57.title: Clement directly addresses the leaders of the sedition, calling them to submit to the presbyters and bend the knees of their hearts.

58.title: He sets life and death before them: those who obey will be enrolled with the holy, those who refuse will inherit ruin.

59.title: Should any disobey the words sent through this letter, let them know they sin against God; Clement begins a great intercessory prayer.

60.title: He prays that God forgive their iniquities, deliver them from those who hate without cause, and lead them to walk in holiness.

61.title: He prays for the rulers and governors that God would guide them in peace and grant them the wisdom to use the authority given to them.

62.title: Clement reviews what he has written: how a godly life is built, how repentance restores, and how love and faith are inseparable.

63.title: He calls on the Corinthians to bend the neck and accept correction, that they may attain the goal set before them.

64.title: A closing benediction that God, ruler of all spirits, may grant his elect every gift of grace through the Lord Jesus Christ.

65.title: Clement asks that the bearers of the letter — Claudius Ephebus, Valerius Bito, and Fortunatus — be sent home swiftly with news of restored peace.
